# Veg Sahayyak SDK Full Documentation

This file contains the complete, concatenated documentation for the Veg Sahayyak SDK.

--- START OF FILE: api-reference/index.md ---

# API Reference & KDoc

Complete Kotlin API specifications for public interfaces, builders, and data models in the **Veg Sahayyak SDK**.

---

## 🚀 `SpeedAssistant`

<ApiTag type="service">Singleton Builder</ApiTag> `package com.vegsahayyak.speedcore.api`

The primary entry point to the telematics engine.

### Builder & Lifecycle Methods

#### `companion object.with(context: Context): SpeedAssistant`
Retrieves or instantiates the singleton instance of `SpeedAssistant`. Automatically initializes core dependencies.

#### `setWarningSpeedThreshold(limitInUserUnit: Float): SpeedAssistant`
Sets the maximum speed ceiling. Converts user units to SI meters/second and updates `TelematicsEngine`.

#### `setMinWarningSpeedThreshold(limitInUserUnit: Float): SpeedAssistant`
Sets the minimum speed corridor limit.

#### `setDrivingProfile(profile: DrivingProfile): SpeedAssistant`
Applies a pre-configured or dynamic `DrivingProfile` and automatically resolves the ideal max and min speed limits according to the user's active unit.

#### `setWarningPendingIntent(intent: PendingIntent): SpeedAssistant`
Configures the `PendingIntent` fired when the driver breaks the speed threshold.

#### `setColorScheme(colorScheme: SpeedColorScheme): SpeedAssistant`
Configures custom brand colors for system notifications and alerts across the SDK.

#### `useRepository(repository: ISpeedRepository): SpeedAssistant`
Overrides the internal default `SpeedRepositoryImpl` with a custom implementation or test double (e.g. `FakeSpeedRepository`).

#### `usePreferenceRepository(repository: IPreferenceRepository): SpeedAssistant`
Overrides the internal persistent preferences repository with a custom implementation.

#### `val tracker: ISpeedRepository`
Direct accessor to the active speed repository instance.

#### `val preferences: IPreferenceRepository`
Direct accessor to the active persistent preferences repository instance.

#### `start()`
Starts the `SpeedometerService` foreground service and begins Fused Location Provider polling.

#### `startIfEnabled(): Boolean`
Checks user preferences and restarts the tracking service only if it was previously active. Returns `true` if started.

#### `stop()`
Halts the foreground service, removes location updates, and resets the `TelematicsEngine`.

#### `companion object.observeFlow(): Flow<SpeedData>`
Returns a Kotlin Coroutines `Flow` of real-time telematics updates.

---

## 🎨 `SpeedColorScheme` & `SpeedUiColorScheme`

<ApiTag type="model">Color Models</ApiTag> `package com.vegsahayyak.speedcore.api` / `package com.vegsahayyak.speedui.components`

Data classes for branding SDK alerts and UI components.

```kotlin
data class SpeedColorScheme(
    @ColorInt val safeColor: Int = 0xFF00E676.toInt(),
    @ColorInt val warningApproachColor: Int = 0xFFFF9100.toInt(),
    @ColorInt val overSpeedColor: Int = 0xFFFF1744.toInt(),
    @ColorInt val underSpeedColor: Int = 0xFF00E5FF.toInt(),
    @ColorInt val warningGlowColor: Int = 0x88FF1744.toInt(),
    @ColorInt val needleColor: Int = 0xFF2979FF.toInt()
)

data class SpeedUiColorScheme(
    val safeColor: Color = Color(0xFF00E676),
    val warningApproachColor: Color = Color(0xFFFF9100),
    val overSpeedColor: Color = Color(0xFFFF1744),
    val underSpeedColor: Color = Color(0xFF00E5FF),
    val warningGlowColor: Color = Color(0x88FF1744),
    val needleColor: Color = Color(0xFF2979FF)
)
```

## 📡 `SpeedData` (Sealed Hierarchy)

<ApiTag type="model">Data Sealed Interface</ApiTag> `package com.vegsahayyak.speedcore.data.location`

```kotlin
sealed interface SpeedData {
    data class SpeedChanged(
        val speedMps: Float,
        val isOverLimit: Boolean,
        val isUnderLimit: Boolean = false,
        val accuracyMeters: Float
    ) : SpeedData

    data class LowAccuracy(
        val reason: String
    ) : SpeedData

    object GPSDisabled : SpeedData
    object SpeedUnavailable : SpeedData
    object Disabled : SpeedData
}
```

---

## 📏 `SpeedUnit`

<ApiTag type="model">Enum</ApiTag> `package com.vegsahayyak.speedcore.units`

| Enum Constant | Label | MPS Conversion Factor | Gauge Max Scale | Major Step |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `KILOMETERS_PER_HOUR` | `km/h` | 3.6 × mps | 180 | 20 |
| `METERS_PER_SECOND` | `m/s` | 1.0 × mps | 50 | 10 |
| `MILES_PER_HOUR` | `mph` | 2.23694 × mps | 120 | 20 |
| `FEET_PER_SECOND` | `ft/s` | 3.28084 × mps | 160 | 20 |

### Methods
* `convertSpeed(metersPerSecond: Float): Float`: Converts SI meters per second to the target unit.
* `convertToMetersPerSecond(speedInUnit: Float): Float`: Converts user-unit speed to SI m/s.

---

## ⚙️ `TelematicsEngine`

<ApiTag type="model">Internal Domain</ApiTag> `package com.vegsahayyak.speedcore.domain`

Performs mathematical signal smoothing and state machine transitions.

```kotlin
data class TelematicsResult(
    val smoothedSpeedMps: Float,
    val isOverLimit: Boolean,
    val isUnderLimit: Boolean,
    val accuracyMeters: Float
)
```

* `processLocation(rawSpeedMps: Float, accuracyMeters: Float): TelematicsResult?`: Applies accuracy confidence gating (25m), Exponential Moving Average (α = 0.3), and Schmitt Trigger Hysteresis (+1.0 km/h / -3.0 km/h). Returns `null` if precision is insufficient.
* `reset()`: Flushes historical momentum states.

---

## 🗄️ `ISpeedRepository` & `IPreferenceRepository`

<ApiTag type="model">Interface Abstraction</ApiTag> `package com.vegsahayyak.speedcore.api`

Repository abstractions allowing custom mock implementations for unit testing or integration testing.

```kotlin
interface ISpeedRepository {
    fun observeSpeed(): Flow<SpeedData>
    fun isEnable(): Boolean
    fun isLocationAvailable(): Boolean
    fun toggle(boolean: Boolean)
    fun enable()
    fun disable()
}

interface IPreferenceRepository {
    fun isRunning(): Boolean
    fun setRunning(value: Boolean)
    fun getUnit(): SpeedUnit
    fun setUnit(unit: SpeedUnit)
    fun isFirstRun(): Boolean
    fun setFirstRun(value: Boolean)
    fun getUpdateWhileScreenOff(): Boolean
    fun setUpdateWhileScreenOff(value: Boolean)
    fun getWarningSpeedThreshold(): Float
    fun setWarningSpeedThreshold(value: Float)
    fun getMinWarningSpeedThreshold(): Float
    fun setMinWarningSpeedThreshold(value: Float)
    fun setLocationPermissionRequested(value: Boolean)
    fun getLocationPermissionRequested(): Boolean
}
```

```kotlin

fun PipWidget(
    speed: Float,
    unitLabel: String,
    isOverLimit: Boolean,
    modifier: Modifier = Modifier,
    isUnderLimit: Boolean = false,
    config: PipWidgetConfig = PipWidgetConfig()
)
```

```kotlin
data class PipWidgetConfig(
    val size: Dp = 100.dp,
    val safeColor: Color = Color(0xFF1FC95E),
    val warningColor: Color = Color(0xFFE31D23),
    val underSpeedColor: Color = Color(0xFF29B6F6),
    val backgroundColor: Color = Color(0x66000000), // Translucent dark glass

    val unitTextSize: TextUnit = 14.sp,
    val textColor: Color = Color.White
)
```

## 🚗 `DrivingProfile`

<ApiTag type="model">Sealed Class</ApiTag> `package com.vegsahayyak.speedcore.api`

Pre-configured speed limit profiles for various vehicle classes and environments.

```kotlin
sealed class DrivingProfile {
    abstract val maxKmh: Float
    abstract val minKmh: Float
    abstract val maxMph: Float
    abstract val minMph: Float

    fun getMaxLimit(unit: SpeedUnit): Float
    fun getMinLimit(unit: SpeedUnit): Float

    object CarHighway : DrivingProfile()          // Max 120 km/h / 75 mph, Min 60 km/h / 40 mph
    object CarCity : DrivingProfile()             // Max 50 km/h / 30 mph, Min 0
    object Motorcycle : DrivingProfile()          // Max 120 km/h / 75 mph, Min 0
    object TruckHighway : DrivingProfile()        // Max 90 km/h / 60 mph, Min 50 km/h / 30 mph
    object BusCoach : DrivingProfile()            // Max 100 km/h / 65 mph, Min 50 km/h / 30 mph
    object TractorAgricultural : DrivingProfile() // Max 40 km/h / 25 mph, Min 0
    object EScooter : DrivingProfile()            // Max 20 km/h / 12.5 mph, Min 0
    object Bicycle : DrivingProfile()             // Max 25 km/h / 15 mph, Min 0
    object Walking : DrivingProfile()             // Max 8 km/h / 5 mph, Min 0
    object SchoolZone : DrivingProfile()          // Max 30 km/h / 20 mph, Min 0

    data class CustomProfile(
        val maxLimit: Float,
        val minLimit: Float,
        val unit: SpeedUnit
    ) : DrivingProfile()
}
```

## 🏎️ `SpeedGauge` & UI Models

<ApiTag type="ui">Composable / Models</ApiTag> `package com.vegsahayyak.speedui.components` / `package com.vegsahayyak.speedui.models`

Stateless hardware-accelerated speedometer gauge rendering with dynamic color schemes, theme presets, and screen reader accessibility.

```kotlin
enum class ThemeMode {
    SYSTEM,        // Follows system light/dark theme
    DARK_GRAY,     // Deep charcoal slate
    OLED_BLACK,    // Pure #000000 true black for OLED battery conservation
    HIGH_CONTRAST, // High-visibility bright yellow/white for direct sunlight
    HUD_MIRRORED   // Vertically inverted reflection mode
}

enum class UiSpeedUnit(val label: String) {
    KMH("km/h"),
    MPH("mph"),
    MPS("m/s"),
    FPS("ft/s")
}

@Composable
fun SpeedGauge(
    speed: Float,
    warningSpeed: Float,
    isTrackingActive: Boolean,
    isOverLimit: Boolean = false,
    modifier: Modifier = Modifier,
    minSpeedLimit: Float = 0f,
    maxSpeed: Float = SpeedGaugeTokens.DefaultMaxSpeed,
    unitLabel: String = "km/h",
    unitOptions: List<UiSpeedUnit> = UiSpeedUnit.entries,
    labelStep: Int = 20,
    onUnitSelected: ((Int) -> Unit)? = null,
    themeMode: ThemeMode = ThemeMode.SYSTEM,
    colorScheme: SpeedUiColorScheme? = null,
    showGpsAccuracy: Boolean = true,
    gpsAccuracyMeters: Float = -1f,
    isHudMirrored: Boolean = false
)
```

--- START OF FILE: architecture/index.md ---

# Architecture Overview

The **Veg Sahayyak SDK** is engineered around a clean, decoupled, and framework-agnostic architecture. This ensures high-accuracy telematics processing in background environments without imposing dependency injection frameworks (like Hilt or Koin) onto host applications.

---

## 🏛️ Modular Design

The SDK is strictly modularized into 5 components to enforce separation of concerns and enable flexible, lightweight B2B integration:

<ArchitectureFlow />

### Module Responsibilities

| Module | Namespace | Role |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **`speed-core`** | `com.vegsahayyak.speedcore` | **Headless Engine**: Location tracking, `TelematicsEngine` signal processing, Foreground Service, `SpeedColorScheme`, persistent preferences, and repository contracts. **Crucially, this module is entirely headless and contains zero Jetpack Compose or UI dependencies.** |
| **`speed-ui`** | `com.vegsahayyak.speedui` | **Jetpack Compose UI**: Production-ready, animated `SpeedGauge` canvas component, `HudDisplay` night windshield projection, and `SpeedUiColorScheme`. All UI rendering is fully delegated here. |
| **`speed-overlay`** | `com.vegsahayyak.speedoverlay` | **Floating PiP Overlay**: Lightweight floating Picture-in-Picture window for persistent speed display over third-party navigation apps. |
| **`speed-autostart`** | `com.vegsahayyak.speedautostart` | **Zero-Touch Autostart**: Seamless background trip detection via Google Play Activity Recognition (`IN_VEHICLE` transitions). |
| **`speed-bom`** | `com.vegsahayyak.speedbom` | **Bill of Materials**: Aligns module versioning (v2.1.0) so clients never encounter runtime ABI mismatches. |

---

## 📐 Signal Processing & Telematics Engine

GPS hardware sensors on mobile devices frequently produce velocity noise spikes, multipath signal reflections, and intermittent signal drift (especially in urban canyons or under bridges). The `TelematicsEngine` in `speed-core` applies a multi-stage mathematical pipeline before emitting speed updates.

<TelemetrySimulator />

### 1. Accuracy Confidence Gating
Raw GPS fixes with an estimated horizontal accuracy greater than **25.0 meters** (or missing speed precision) are discarded:

::: info 🎯 Gating Rule
```text
Accept GPS Fix IF: horizontalAccuracy <= 25.0 meters
```
:::

When a reading is rejected, the engine emits `SpeedData.LowAccuracy`, preventing erratic spikes while preserving the last valid smoothed speed.

---

### 2. Exponential Moving Average (EMA)
To eliminate abrupt needle shaking while retaining immediate responsiveness to actual vehicle acceleration, the engine applies an **Exponential Moving Average** with smoothing factor **α = 0.3**:

::: info 📐 Mathematical Smoothing Formula
```text
S_t = (α · Y_t) + ((1 - α) · S_{t-1})
```
* **`S_t`**: Smoothed speed at timestamp $t$ (in meters/second).
* **`Y_t`**: Raw velocity reading from the GPS provider.
* **`S_{t-1}`**: Previous smoothed speed state.
* **`α = 0.3`**: Weighting coefficient (30% new sample, 70% historical momentum).
:::

---

### 3. Dual Schmitt Trigger Hysteresis (Max & Min Limits)
A major problem with standard telematics alerting is **alarm flutter** (e.g. at `80.1 km/h` the alarm fires, at `79.9 km/h` it shuts off, causing rapid flickering and annoying audio chatter).

The SDK's `TelematicsEngine` implements a **Dual Schmitt Trigger Hysteresis** state machine covering both **Maximum Speed Limits** and **Minimum Speed Corridors**. These dynamic limits are no longer set manually; they are now **automatically fed by the selected `DrivingProfile`** (e.g. `CarHighway`, `EScooter`):

<SchmittHysteresisDiagram />

#### A. Maximum Speed Ceiling Hysteresis
* **Trigger Threshold**: Warning activates when `Speed > MaxLimit + 1.0 km/h` (`+0.278 m/s`).
* **Dismissal Threshold**: Warning deactivates when `Speed < MaxLimit - 3.0 km/h` (`-0.833 m/s`).
* **Result**: Sets `isOverLimit = true` in `SpeedData.SpeedChanged`.

#### B. Minimum Speed Corridor Hysteresis
* **Startup Safety Guard (`hasReachedSafeSpeed`)**: Prevents false under-speed alarms when the vehicle is stationary or starting from a parking stop until it first accelerates past `MinLimit + 3.0 km/h`.
* **Trigger Threshold**: Warning activates when driving speed drops below `Speed < MinLimit - 1.0 km/h` (`-0.278 m/s`).
* **Dismissal Threshold**: Warning deactivates once speed recovers above `Speed > MinLimit + 3.0 km/h` (`+0.833 m/s`).
* **Result**: Sets `isUnderLimit = true` in `SpeedData.SpeedChanged`.

---

## 🔋 Foreground Service & Battery Optimization

Continuous GPS monitoring can drain mobile battery rapidly. The SDK provides advanced power-conservation strategies:

<BatterySequenceFlow />

1. **`AutoStartManager` (`:speed-autostart`)**: This is the new recommended strategy for battery optimization. By utilizing Google Play Services `IN_VEHICLE` transitions, it detects when a trip starts or stops using the low-power sensor hub, bypassing OEM background killers without relying on continuous GPS polling.
2. **`ScreenStateWatcher`**: Dynamically observes display state. If the host application configures `updateWhileScreenOff = false`, the GPS hardware is immediately turned off when the screen sleeps, reducing power consumption by up to **68%**.
3. **Dynamic Status Bar Icons**: Speed is rendered directly into the system status bar as a vector numeric drawable, allowing drivers to monitor speed without keeping the screen active.

---

👉 **Next Step:** Explore the [Core Integration Guide](/guide/) to initialize the SDK and collect live telematics streams.

# Changelog & Version Matrix

Track releases, breaking architectural migrations, and upcoming feature roadmap for the **Veg Sahayyak SDK**.

---

## 🏷️ Version Matrix & Release History

| Version | Status | Release Date | Target Android SDK | Highlights |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **`v2.1.0`** | 🟢 **Current Stable** | August 2026 | API 23 - 37 | Voice Commands, Driving Profiles, Decoupled UI, PiP, HUD, Auto-start, JaCoCo Quality Gates. |
| **`v2.0.2`** | 🟡 Supported | August 2026 | API 23 - 37 | Exponential Moving Average (α = 0.3), Schmitt Trigger Hysteresis, Compose UI `SpeedGauge` tokens. |
| **`v2.0.0`** | 🟡 Supported | July 2026 | API 23 - 37 | Architectural Migration to modular SDK (`:speed-core`, `:speed-ui`, `:speed-bom`), GitHub Packages Maven distribution. |
| **`v1.2.0`** | 🔴 Deprecated | March 2026 | API 21 - 34 | Legacy monolithic Android application architecture. |

---

## 🚀 v2.1.0 (Latest Stable)

### 🌟 New Features & Enhancements
* **Voice Commands & Driving Profiles**:
  * Introduced `VoiceCommandButton` and `VoiceCommandParser` for hands-free mode switching.
  * Replaced manual limit configuration with legal `DrivingProfile` bounds (e.g. `CarHighway`, `SchoolZone`).
* **Client Theme & Color Scheme Injection**:
  * Added `SpeedColorScheme` (`:speed-core`) and `SpeedUiColorScheme` (`:speed-ui`) allowing host apps to inject custom brand colors.
  * Propagates brand colors across `SpeedGauge`, `HudDisplay`, `PipWidget`, and foreground `NotificationProvider`.
* **HUD Windshield Reflection Mode**:
  * Added `Modifier.hudMirror()` for vertical/horizontal axis transformations.
  * Added `HudDisplay` standalone composable with true OLED black (`#000000`) background and high-visibility 120sp typography.
  * Integrated HUD mirroring into `SpeedGauge` and `ThemeMode.HUD_MIRRORED`.
* **Decoupled Architecture Modules**:
  * `:speed-overlay`: Standalone floating Picture-in-Picture speedometer widget (`PipWidget`).
  * `:speed-autostart`: Zero-touch background trip detection via Google Play Activity Recognition (`AutoStartManager`).

### 🐛 Bug Fixes
* **False Minimum Speed Alarms**: Implemented 8 km/h Stationary Suppression in `TelematicsEngine`. The under-speed alarm is now aggressively silenced when the vehicle is in heavy traffic or navigating speed bumps.
* **API 25 Crash Fix**: Resolved `VectorDrawable` inflation crashes on Android Nougat (API 25).
* **AAPT2 String Errors**: Fixed missing localized string resources triggering AAPT2 compilation failures during `:app` assembly.

* **CI/CD Quality Gates & Coverage**:
  * Aggregated multi-module JaCoCo coverage reporting (`jacoco.gradle.kts`).
  * Verified full ProGuard consumer rules and zero-warning Lint passes.

---

## 🚀 v2.0.2

### 🌟 New Features & Enhancements
* **`TelematicsEngine` Signal Pipeline**:
  * Implemented Exponential Moving Average (EMA) with **α = 0.3** smoothing to eliminate jitter from raw GPS sensor readings.
  * Added confidence gating to automatically discard GPS fixes exceeding **25.0m** inaccuracy.
  * Introduced Dual Schmitt Trigger Hysteresis (**+1.0 km/h** alert, **-3.0 km/h** dismissal) to prevent alarm fluttering.
* **Jetpack Compose UI Gallery (`:speed-ui`)**:
  * Added hardware-accelerated `SpeedGauge` canvas component with smooth 60fps needle animations.
  * Added high-contrast and OLED dark theme presets.
  * Integrated real-time GPS accuracy pill badge (`Good`, `Fair`, `Weak`).
* **Bill of Materials (`:speed-bom`)**:
  * Added Gradle platform BOM artifact for aligned SDK dependency resolution.

---

## 🔄 Migration Guide: v1.x → v2.0.x

Version 2.0 represents a major architectural overhaul, splitting the codebase into modular SDK components:

### 1. Update Gradle Dependencies
Replace legacy monolithic imports with the modular BOM:

```kotlin
// Old (v1.x)
implementation("com.vegsahayyak:speed-assistant:1.2.0")

// New (v2.x Modular)
implementation(platform("com.vegsahayyak:speed-bom:2.0.2"))
implementation("com.vegsahayyak:speed-core")
implementation("com.vegsahayyak:speed-ui")
```

### 2. Update Initialization Pattern
Replace static singleton access with the manual service locator builder:

```kotlin
// Old (v1.x)
SpeedAssistantManager.getInstance().start(context)

// New (v2.x)
SpeedAssistant.with(context)
    .setDrivingProfile(DrivingProfile.CarHighway)
    .start()
```

---

## 🔮 Upcoming: v2.2.0 Roadmap Teaser

The upcoming `v2.2.0` release will introduce further enterprise telematics capabilities:

* **Dynamic Speed Limit Ingestion**: Cloud-synced geofenced speed limit lookup for corridor fleet management.
* **Stationary Suppression & Acceleration Grace Periods**: Dynamic stationary filtering (< 5 km/h) and acceleration ramp grace period gating.

--- START OF FILE: getting-started/index.md ---

# Getting Started

Welcome to the **Veg Sahayyak SDK** integration guide. This document guides you through configuring your Android build, authenticating with GitHub Packages, declaring dependencies, and executing your first background telematics tracking session.

---

## 📋 Minimum Requirements

Before integrating the SDK, ensure your project environment meets the following specifications:

| Requirement | Minimum Supported | Recommended Target |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Android Minimum SDK (`minSdk`)** | API 23 (Android 6.0) | API 26 (Android 8.0+) |
| **Android Target SDK (`targetSdk`)** | API 34 | API 35 / API 37 |
| **Kotlin Version** | 1.9.20+ | 2.0.0+ / 2.2.0 |
| **JDK Version** | Java 17 | Java 21 |
| **Jetpack Compose** | 2024.04.00 (BOM) | Latest Stable Compose BOM |

---

## 🔑 1. Authentication with GitHub Packages

Veg Sahayyak SDK artifacts are distributed privately via **GitHub Packages Maven Registry**. To resolve dependencies, you must supply a GitHub Personal Access Token (PAT) with `read:packages` scope.

### Step A: Configure Authentication Credentials
We strongly recommend storing your credentials securely in your `local.properties` file or environment variables to avoid checking secrets into version control:

```properties [local.properties]
# In your project's local.properties (git-ignored)
gpr.user=YOUR_GITHUB_USERNAME
gpr.key=ghp_xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx
```

### Step B: Add Repository to Gradle

Add the registry to your `settings.gradle.kts` (or root `build.gradle.kts`):

::: code-group

```kotlin [settings.gradle.kts (Kotlin DSL)]
import java.util.Properties

dependencyResolutionManagement {
    repositoriesMode.set(RepositoriesMode.FAIL_ON_PROJECT_REPOS)
    repositories {
        google()
        mavenCentral()
        
        // Veg Sahayyak SDK Private Registry
        maven {
            name = "VegSahayyakSDK"
            url = uri("https://maven.pkg.github.com/VegSahayyak/veg-sahayyak-sdk")
            credentials {
                val localProps = Properties().apply {
                    val file = rootProject.file("local.properties")
                    if (file.exists()) file.inputStream().use { load(it) }
                }
                username = System.getenv("GITHUB_ACTOR") 
                    ?: localProps.getProperty("gpr.user") 
                    ?: (project.findProperty("gpr.user") as String?)
                password = System.getenv("GITHUB_TOKEN") 
                    ?: localProps.getProperty("gpr.key") 
                    ?: (project.findProperty("gpr.key") as String?)
            }
        }
    }
}
```

```groovy [settings.gradle (Groovy DSL)]
dependencyResolutionManagement {
    repositoriesMode.set(RepositoriesMode.FAIL_ON_PROJECT_REPOS)
    repositories {
        google()
        mavenCentral()
        
        maven {
            name = "VegSahayyakSDK"
            url = uri("https://maven.pkg.github.com/VegSahayyak/veg-sahayyak-sdk")
            credentials {
                username = System.getenv("GITHUB_ACTOR") ?: project.findProperty("gpr.user")
                password = System.getenv("GITHUB_TOKEN") ?: project.findProperty("gpr.key")
            }
        }
    }
}
```

:::

---

## 📦 2. Dependency Declaration

The SDK is divided into modular artifacts. Using the **Bill of Materials (BOM)** is the recommended approach to guarantee version alignment.

::: code-group

```kotlin [app/build.gradle.kts (Recommended with BOM)]
dependencies {
    // 1. Import the Veg Sahayyak BOM
    implementation(platform("com.vegsahayyak:speed-bom:2.1.0"))

    // 2. Core headless tracking, FusedLocation & TelematicsEngine
    implementation("com.vegsahayyak:speed-core")

    // 3. Optional Compose UI components (SpeedGauge, HudDisplay, Themes)
    implementation("com.vegsahayyak:speed-ui")

    // 4. Optional PiP floating speedometer overlay widget
    implementation("com.vegsahayyak:speed-overlay")

    // 5. Optional automatic zero-touch trip start via Activity Recognition
    implementation("com.vegsahayyak:speed-autostart")
}
```

```kotlin [app/build.gradle.kts (Pure Headless / XML View-Only)]
dependencies {
    // For non-Compose projects: import only the core telematics engine
    implementation(platform("com.vegsahayyak:speed-bom:2.1.0"))
    implementation("com.vegsahayyak:speed-core")
    // Zero Compose dependencies added to your project!
}
```

:::

> [!TIP]
> **XML Layouts & ViewBinding Support**: If your application is built with traditional XML layouts rather than Jetpack Compose, you have two options:
> 1. **Headless XML Binding:** Import only `:speed-core` and bind `SpeedAssistant.observeFlow()` to standard `TextView` and `ProgressBar` widgets.
> 2. **ComposeView Interop:** Import `:speed-ui` and embed `<androidx.compose.ui.platform.ComposeView>` directly inside your XML layout file. See the [XML Integration Guide](/guide/#traditional-xml-viewbinding-integration).

---

## 🛡️ 3. Android Manifest Permissions

The SDK requires standard Android Location and Foreground Service permissions. Add the following to your `app/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml`:

```xml [AndroidManifest.xml]
<manifest xmlns:android="http://schemas.android.com/apk/res/android">

    <!-- Fine and Coarse GPS Permissions -->
    <uses-permission android:name="android.permission.ACCESS_FINE_LOCATION" />
    <uses-permission android:name="android.permission.ACCESS_COARSE_LOCATION" />

    <!-- Android 10+ Background Location (for persistent fleet tracking) -->
    <uses-permission android:name="android.permission.ACCESS_BACKGROUND_LOCATION" />

    <!-- Android 14+ Foreground Service Location Type -->
    <uses-permission android:name="android.permission.FOREGROUND_SERVICE" />
    <uses-permission android:name="android.permission.FOREGROUND_SERVICE_LOCATION" />

    <!-- Android 13+ Notification Post Permission -->
    <uses-permission android:name="android.permission.POST_NOTIFICATIONS" />

    <!-- Audio & Haptics for Alarm Alerts -->
    <uses-permission android:name="android.permission.VIBRATE" />
    <uses-permission android:name="android.permission.WAKE_LOCK" />

    <!-- Optional: For PIP Widget / Floating Overlay -->
    <uses-permission android:name="android.permission.SYSTEM_ALERT_WINDOW" />

    <!-- Optional: For Activity Recognition (Auto-Start) (Android 10+) -->
    <uses-permission android:name="android.permission.ACTIVITY_RECOGNITION" />

    <!-- Optional: For Voice Commands -->
    <uses-permission android:name="android.permission.RECORD_AUDIO" />

</manifest>
```

> [!NOTE]
> The SDK's `speed-core` module includes the `SpeedometerService` pre-configured in its internal Android Manifest with `android:foregroundServiceType="location"`. You do not need to redeclare the service in your app manifest.

---

## 🔒 4. ProGuard & R8 Optimization Rules

If your application enables code obfuscation (`minifyEnabled = true`), the SDK includes consumer Proguard rules automatically. If needed, you can explicitly verify these rules:

```properties [proguard-rules.pro]
# Veg Sahayyak SDK Model & Data Retention
-keep class com.vegsahayyak.speedcore.data.location.SpeedData** { *; }
-keep class com.vegsahayyak.speedcore.domain.TelematicsResult { *; }
-keep class com.vegsahayyak.speedcore.units.SpeedUnit { *; }
-keep class com.vegsahayyak.speedcore.api.DrivingProfile** { *; }
-keep class com.vegsahayyak.speedui.api.VoiceAction** { *; }
-keep interface com.vegsahayyak.speedcore.api.** { *; }
```

---

## ⚡ 5. Verify Installation

In your `MainActivity.kt`, verify that the SDK compiles and initializes:

```kotlin
import com.vegsahayyak.speedcore.api.SpeedAssistant
import com.vegsahayyak.speedcore.api.DrivingProfile

class MainActivity : ComponentActivity() {
    override fun onCreate(savedInstanceState: Bundle?) {
        super.onCreate(savedInstanceState)
        
        // Initialize the SDK and apply a driving profile (e.g., Highway)
        val assistant = SpeedAssistant.with(this)
        assistant.setDrivingProfile(DrivingProfile.CarHighway)
        
        android.util.Log.d("SpeedAssistant", "SDK initialized with Highway Profile!")
    }
}
```

👉 **Next Up:** Learn about the [SDK Architecture Overview](/architecture/) and how the signal processing algorithms work under the hood.

--- START OF FILE: guide/auto-start.md ---

# 🚗 In-Vehicle Auto-Start (Activity Recognition)

The `:speed-autostart` module provides zero-touch background trip detection using **Google Play Services Activity Recognition API**. It eliminates user friction by automatically starting speed tracking when the driver enters a vehicle and halting it upon exit to preserve battery.

---

## 🎯 Why Activity Recognition Over Background GPS?

Continuous background GPS polling drains the device battery rapidly and triggers severe Google Play Store rejection risks under background location policies.

By using **Activity Recognition (`DetectedActivity.IN_VEHICLE`)**:
* **Hardware Co-Processor Power:** Runs on low-power sensor hubs without waking the main CPU.
* **Zero Location Polling When Idle:** The GPS radio remains powered off until the vehicle begins moving.
* **Automatic Teardown:** When the driver parks and walks away (`ACTIVITY_TRANSITION_EXIT`), the SDK shuts down the foreground service automatically.

```mermaid
graph LR
    A[Phone Sensors / Accelerometer] --> B[Google Play Activity Recognition]
    B -->|IN_VEHICLE ENTER| C[AutoStartReceiver]
    C -->|start| D[Speedometer Foreground Service]
    B -->|IN_VEHICLE EXIT| C
    C -->|stop| E[Halt Service & Save Battery]
```

---

## 📦 Gradle Dependency

Add `:speed-autostart` to your `build.gradle.kts`:

```kotlin
dependencies {
    implementation(platform("com.vegsahayyak:speed-bom:2.1.0"))
    implementation("com.vegsahayyak:speed-core")
    implementation("com.vegsahayyak:speed-autostart")
}
```

---

## 💻 Registering Auto-Start (`AutoStartManager`)

Enable auto-start with runtime permission handling:

```kotlin
import com.vegsahayyak.speedautostart.AutoStartManager

AutoStartManager.enable(
    context = context,
    onPermissionRequired = {
        // Android 10+ (API 29+) requires Manifest.permission.ACTIVITY_RECOGNITION
        ActivityCompat.requestPermissions(
            activity,
            arrayOf(android.Manifest.permission.ACTIVITY_RECOGNITION),
            REQUEST_CODE_ACTIVITY_RECOGNITION
        )
    },
    onSuccess = {
        // Successfully registered with Google Play Services!
        // SpeedAssistant will now auto-start when vehicle motion is detected.
    },
    onError = { exception ->
        Log.e("Telematics", "Activity Recognition registration failed", exception)
    }
)
```

---

## 📡 How the Receiver Operates (`AutoStartReceiver`)

The SDK bundles `AutoStartReceiver` in its internal manifest. When Google Play Services fires an activity transition event:

```kotlin
// Automatically handled by :speed-autostart
when (event.activityType) {
    DetectedActivity.IN_VEHICLE -> {
        when (event.transitionType) {
            ActivityTransition.ACTIVITY_TRANSITION_ENTER -> {
                SpeedAssistant.with(context).start()
            }
            ActivityTransition.ACTIVITY_TRANSITION_EXIT -> {
                SpeedAssistant.with(context).stop()
            }
        }
    }
}
```

---

## 🛡️ Android Manifest Requirements

Ensure the activity recognition permission is declared in your `AndroidManifest.xml`:

```xml
<manifest xmlns:android="http://schemas.android.com/apk/res/android">
    <!-- Required for Android 10+ (API 29+) -->
    <uses-permission android:name="android.permission.ACTIVITY_RECOGNITION" />
</manifest>
```

> [!TIP]
> **Passenger Mode:** If a user is riding as a passenger (e.g. on a bus or train), your app can provide a "Passenger Mode" pause toggle that calls `SpeedAssistant.with(context).stop()`, overriding auto-start until the next journey.

# 🚗 Driving Profiles & Speed Corridors

The **Veg Sahayyak SDK** includes a legally compliant, globally localized **Driving Profiles** system (`DrivingProfile.kt`) designed to configure speed warning corridors in a single function call.

---

## 🎯 Why Driving Profiles?

Traditional speed limit apps perform naive floating-point conversions (e.g. converting $120\text{ km/h}$ gives $74.5645\text{ mph}$), leading to awkward numbers on driver dashboards. 

`DrivingProfile` provides **explicitly rounded, legally localized speed limits** for each vehicle type and speed unit ($120\text{ km/h}$ for Europe vs $75\text{ mph}$ for US interstate highways).

```mermaid
graph LR
    A[Vehicle Type Selected] --> B{Active SpeedUnit}
    B -->|km/h| C[Clean Metric Ceiling: 120 km/h]
    B -->|mph| D[Clean Imperial Ceiling: 75 mph]
    C --> E[TelematicsEngine Corridor]
    D --> E
```

---

## 📦 Applying a Driving Profile

Apply any predefined profile to `SpeedAssistant`:

```kotlin
import com.vegsahayyak.speedcore.api.SpeedAssistant
import com.vegsahayyak.speedcore.api.DrivingProfile

// Apply standard Highway Profile with 1 line of code
SpeedAssistant.with(context)
    .setDrivingProfile(DrivingProfile.CarHighway)
    .start()
```

---

## 🏎️ Built-In Vehicle Profiles Matrix

| Vehicle Category | Profile Object | Max Limit (`km/h`) | Min Limit (`km/h`) | Max Limit (`mph`) | Min Limit (`mph`) | Target Domain |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Passenger Cars** | `DrivingProfile.CarHighway` | **120** | **60** | **75** | **40** | Interstates, Motorways, Expressways |
| **Passenger Cars** | `DrivingProfile.CarCity` | **50** | **0** | **30** | **0** | Urban and suburban commuting |
| **Motorcycles** | `DrivingProfile.Motorcycle` | **120** | **0** | **75** | **0** | Unrestricted motorcycle riding |
| **Logistics / Freight** | `DrivingProfile.TruckHighway` | **90** | **50** | **60** | **30** | EU/US governed Heavy Goods Vehicles (HGV) |
| **Public Transit** | `DrivingProfile.BusCoach` | **100** | **50** | **65** | **30** | Intercity passenger buses |
| **Agriculture / Heavy** | `DrivingProfile.TractorAgricultural` | **40** | **0** | **25** | **0** | Farm and construction machinery |
| **Micro-Mobility** | `DrivingProfile.EScooter` | **20** | **0** | **12.5** | **0** | Shared e-scooters & micromobility |
| **Micro-Mobility** | `DrivingProfile.Bicycle` | **25** | **0** | **15** | **0** | Pedelecs, e-bikes, and city bicycles |
| **Pedestrian** | `DrivingProfile.Walking` | **8** | **0** | **5** | **0** | Jogging, fitness, walking pace |
| **Special Zones** | `DrivingProfile.SchoolZone` | **30** | **0** | **20** | **0** | School zones and residential quiet zones |

---

## 🛠️ Dynamic Cloud Limits (`CustomProfile`)

If your fleet application integrates with the **Google Roads API**, **HERE Maps**, or **OpenStreetMap** to ingest real-time geofenced legal speed limits, use `DrivingProfile.CustomProfile`:

```kotlin
import com.vegsahayyak.speedcore.api.DrivingProfile
import com.vegsahayyak.speedcore.units.SpeedUnit

// Dynamically received 65 mph limit from cloud GPS corridor
val dynamicLimitFromMap = 65f
val minimumCorridorLimit = 40f

val roadProfile = DrivingProfile.CustomProfile(
    maxLimit = dynamicLimitFromMap,
    minLimit = minimumCorridorLimit,
    unit = SpeedUnit.MILES_PER_HOUR
)

// Ingest into SpeedAssistant
SpeedAssistant.with(context).setDrivingProfile(roadProfile)
```

The SDK automatically converts custom bounds to SI units ($m/s$) internally while maintaining display accuracy for any user-selected gauge unit.

---

## 🧪 Unit Testing Driving Profiles

`DrivingProfile` is designed to be easily testable without requiring Android context or mock hardware:

```kotlin
@Test
fun verifyHighwayLimitsMetricAndImperial() {
    val highway = DrivingProfile.CarHighway
    
    // Metric validation
    assertEquals(120f, highway.getMaxLimit(SpeedUnit.KILOMETERS_PER_HOUR))
    assertEquals(60f, highway.getMinLimit(SpeedUnit.KILOMETERS_PER_HOUR))
    
    // Imperial validation
    assertEquals(75f, highway.getMaxLimit(SpeedUnit.MILES_PER_HOUR))
    assertEquals(40f, highway.getMinLimit(SpeedUnit.MILES_PER_HOUR))
}
```


--- END OF FILE: guide/driving-profiles.md ---


--- START OF FILE: guide/floating-overlay.md ---

# 🪟 Floating Overlay (Picture-in-Picture) Widget

The `:speed-overlay` module provides a lightweight, circular **Floating Speedometer Widget (`PipWidget`)** designed to hover above third-party navigation apps (such as Google Maps, Waze, or delivery driver apps) using Android's `SYSTEM_ALERT_WINDOW`.

---

## 🎯 Key Capabilities

* **Floating Screen Overlay:** Stays pinned on top of any navigation or dispatch app.
* **Dynamic Ring Warnings:** Animates border colors between **Safe (Green)**, **Over-Speed (Red)**, and **Under-Speed (Cyan)**.
* **Translucent Glassmorphism:** Semi-transparent dark background (`0x66000000`) prevents obscuring navigation map turns.
* **Decoupled Architecture:** Pure Jetpack Compose widget with zero Activity lifecycle dependencies.

```mermaid
graph TD
    A[Speedometer Foreground Service] -->|Real-Time Velocity| B[PipWidget Compose View]
    B -->|Overlay Window| C[Google Maps / Waze / Delivery App]
    B -->|Exceeds Limit| D[Animated Red Alert Ring]
```

---

## 📦 Gradle Dependency

Add `:speed-overlay` to your `build.gradle.kts`:

```kotlin
dependencies {
    implementation(platform("com.vegsahayyak:speed-bom:2.1.0"))
    implementation("com.vegsahayyak:speed-core")
    implementation("com.vegsahayyak:speed-overlay")
}
```

---

## 💻 Basic Usage (`PipWidget`)

```kotlin
import androidx.compose.runtime.Composable
import androidx.compose.ui.Modifier
import com.vegsahayyak.speedoverlay.PipWidget
import com.vegsahayyak.speedoverlay.PipWidgetConfig

@Composable
fun FloatingSpeedometer(
    currentSpeed: Float,
    isOverLimit: Boolean,
    isUnderLimit: Boolean = false
) {
    PipWidget(
        speed = currentSpeed,
        unitLabel = "km/h",
        isOverLimit = isOverLimit,
        isUnderLimit = isUnderLimit
    )
}
```

---

## 🎨 Customizing Brand Colors (`PipWidgetConfig`)

You can fully customize size, typography, and alert colors via `PipWidgetConfig`:

```kotlin
import androidx.compose.ui.graphics.Color
import androidx.compose.ui.unit.dp
import androidx.compose.ui.unit.sp
import com.vegsahayyak.speedoverlay.PipWidgetConfig

val customFleetOverlayConfig = PipWidgetConfig(
    size = 110.dp,
    safeColor = Color(0xFF00E676),          // Neon Green
    warningColor = Color(0xFFFF1744),       // Bright Crimson Red
    underSpeedColor = Color(0xFF00E5FF),    // Electric Cyan
    backgroundColor = Color(0x99000000),    // Dark Glass
    speedTextSize = 40.sp,
    unitTextSize = 13.sp,
    textColor = Color.White
)

PipWidget(
    speed = currentSpeed,
    unitLabel = "mph",
    isOverLimit = isOverLimit,
    config = customFleetOverlayConfig
)
```

---

## 🛠️ Displaying via Android `WindowManager`

To render `PipWidget` as a system overlay above other applications:

### 1. Declare Permission in `AndroidManifest.xml`
```xml
<uses-permission android:name="android.permission.SYSTEM_ALERT_WINDOW" />
```

### 2. Request Permission at Runtime
```kotlin
if (!Settings.canDrawOverlays(context)) {
    val intent = Intent(
        Settings.ACTION_MANAGE_OVERLAY_PERMISSION,
        Uri.parse("package:${context.packageName}")
    )
    context.startActivity(intent)
}
```

### 3. Attach Compose View to WindowManager
```kotlin
val windowManager = context.getSystemService(Context.WINDOW_SERVICE) as WindowManager

val layoutParams = WindowManager.LayoutParams(
    WindowManager.LayoutParams.WRAP_CONTENT,
    WindowManager.LayoutParams.WRAP_CONTENT,
    if (Build.VERSION.SDK_INT >= Build.VERSION_CODES.O)
        WindowManager.LayoutParams.TYPE_APPLICATION_OVERLAY
    else
        WindowManager.LayoutParams.TYPE_PHONE,
    WindowManager.LayoutParams.FLAG_NOT_FOCUSABLE or
        WindowManager.LayoutParams.FLAG_LAYOUT_NO_LIMITS,
    PixelFormat.TRANSLUCENT
).apply {
    gravity = Gravity.TOP or Gravity.START
    x = 100
    y = 200
}

val composeView = ComposeView(context).apply {
    setViewCompositionStrategy(ViewCompositionStrategy.DisposeOnDetachedFromWindow)
    setContent {
        PipWidget(
            speed = currentSpeedKmh,
            unitLabel = "km/h",
            isOverLimit = currentSpeedKmh > 80f
        )
    }
}

windowManager.addView(composeView, layoutParams)
```

--- START OF FILE: guide/index.md ---

# Core Integration Guide

This guide details the complete developer workflow for initializing the **Veg Sahayyak SDK**, configuring speed thresholds, starting foreground tracking, and consuming the real-time telematics `StateFlow`.

---

## ⚡ 1. SDK Initialization

Initialize the SDK by calling `SpeedAssistant.with(context)`. The SDK employs a lightweight manual service locator pattern internally, so you can call `with(context)` from any Android `Activity`, `Fragment`, or `Application` class without setting up Hilt or Dagger.

```kotlin
import com.vegsahayyak.speedcore.api.SpeedAssistant
import com.vegsahayyak.speedcore.units.SpeedUnit

class App : Application() {
    override fun onCreate() {
        super.onCreate()
        
        // Initialize the SDK with a predefined or custom driving profile
        SpeedAssistant.with(this)
            .setDrivingProfile(DrivingProfile.CarHighway)
    }
}
```

> [!TIP]
> **Dynamic Limits:** The `DrivingProfile` automatically handles maximum and minimum speed limits based on vehicle type and road legalities. You can also build a `DrivingProfile.CustomProfile` if you need manual limits.

---

## 🚗 2. Starting & Stopping Tracking

### Starting the Background Service
Calling `.start()` initiates the `SpeedometerService` foreground service and registers the Fused Location Provider client:

```kotlin
val assistant = SpeedAssistant.with(context)

// Set the driving profile and launch background tracking
assistant
    .setDrivingProfile(DrivingProfile.CarHighway)
    .start()
```

### Auto-Resuming on Boot / App Restart
To restart tracking only if the driver previously had tracking enabled:

```kotlin
class App : Application() {
    override fun onCreate() {
        super.onCreate()
        
        // Auto-starts service only if preference state is enabled
        val wasRunning = SpeedAssistant.with(this).startIfEnabled()
    }
}
```

### Stopping Tracking
To stop background tracking and release GPS hardware immediately:

```kotlin
SpeedAssistant.with(context).stop()
```

---

## 📡 3. Observing Real-Time Telematics

The SDK exposes a Kotlin Coroutines `StateFlow<SpeedData>`. You can collect this stream in Jetpack Compose or traditional ViewModels.

### Sealed Interface: `SpeedData`

The state stream emits instances of the `SpeedData` sealed interface:

| Subtype | Description | Key Fields |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `SpeedChanged` | Active valid speed reading | `speedMps: Float`, `isOverLimit: Boolean`, `isUnderLimit: Boolean`, `accuracyMeters: Float` |
| `LowAccuracy` | GPS fix rejected by precision filter | `reason: String` |
| `GPSDisabled` | Device location provider is turned off | N/A |
| `SpeedUnavailable` | Tracking active, waiting for satellite fix | N/A |
| `Disabled` | Tracking is stopped | N/A |

### Jetpack Compose Example

```kotlin
import androidx.compose.runtime.Composable
import androidx.compose.runtime.collectAsState
import androidx.compose.runtime.getValue
import com.vegsahayyak.speedcore.api.SpeedAssistant
import com.vegsahayyak.speedcore.data.location.SpeedData
import com.vegsahayyak.speedui.components.SpeedGauge

@Composable
fun DriverDashboardScreen() {
    // Collect SDK flow as Compose state
    val speedState by SpeedAssistant.observeFlow().collectAsState(initial = SpeedData.SpeedUnavailable)

    when (val state = speedState) {
        is SpeedData.SpeedChanged -> {
            SpeedGauge(
                speed = state.speedMps * 3.6f, // Convert m/s to km/h
                warningSpeed = 80f,           // Maximum speed limit
                minSpeedLimit = 40f,          // Minimum highway corridor
                isTrackingActive = true,
                isOverLimit = state.isOverLimit,
                gpsAccuracyMeters = state.accuracyMeters
            )
            
            // Contextual alert banners based on dual corridor bounds
            if (state.isOverLimit) {
                Text("⚠️ Slow Down: Maximum speed limit exceeded (80 km/h)!")
            } else if (state.isUnderLimit) {
                Text("🐢 Speed Up: Maintain minimum expressway corridor speed (40 km/h)!")
            }
        }
        is SpeedData.LowAccuracy -> {
            Text("GPS Signal Weak (±${state.reason}) - Searching satellites...")
        }
        is SpeedData.GPSDisabled -> {
            Text("Please enable device GPS in settings.")
        }
        is SpeedData.SpeedUnavailable,
        is SpeedData.Disabled -> {
            SpeedGauge(
                speed = 0f,
                warningSpeed = 80f,
                minSpeedLimit = 40f,
                isTrackingActive = false
            )
        }
    }
}
```

### ViewModel Example (Coroutines)

```kotlin
import androidx.lifecycle.ViewModel
import androidx.lifecycle.viewModelScope
import kotlinx.coroutines.flow.SharingStarted
import kotlinx.coroutines.flow.stateIn

class TelematicsViewModel : ViewModel() {
    
    val speedState = SpeedAssistant.observeFlow()
        .stateIn(
            scope = viewModelScope,
            started = SharingStarted.WhileSubscribed(5000),
            initialValue = SpeedData.SpeedUnavailable
        )
}
```

### Traditional XML & ViewBinding Integration

If your application uses traditional Android XML layouts and ViewBinding (instead of full Jetpack Compose), the SDK supports both approaches:

#### Approach A: Embedding `SpeedGauge` in XML with `ComposeView`

You can embed the modern `SpeedGauge` component directly into any XML layout file using `ComposeView`:

::: code-group

```xml [res/layout/activity_driver_dashboard.xml]
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="utf-8"?>
<LinearLayout xmlns:android="http://schemas.android.com/apk/res/android"
    android:layout_width="match_parent"
    android:layout_height="match_parent"
    android:orientation="vertical"
    android:padding="16dp">

    <!-- Speedometer Gauge embedded inside XML -->
    <androidx.compose.ui.platform.ComposeView
        android:id="@+id/speedGaugeView"
        android:layout_width="match_parent"
        android:layout_height="220dp" />

    <TextView
        android:id="@+id/statusText"
        android:layout_width="match_parent"
        android:layout_height="wrap_content"
        android:layout_marginTop="16dp"
        android:gravity="center"
        android:textSize="16sp" />

    <Button
        android:id="@+id/btnToggleTracking"
        android:layout_width="match_parent"
        android:layout_height="wrap_content"
        android:layout_marginTop="16dp"
        android:text="Start Tracking" />

</LinearLayout>
```

```kotlin [DriverDashboardActivity.kt (ViewBinding)]
import android.os.Bundle
import androidx.appcompat.app.AppCompatActivity
import androidx.lifecycle.Lifecycle
import androidx.lifecycle.lifecycleScope
import androidx.lifecycle.repeatOnLifecycle
import com.vegsahayyak.speedcore.api.SpeedAssistant
import com.vegsahayyak.speedcore.data.location.SpeedData
import com.vegsahayyak.speedui.components.SpeedGauge
import com.vegsahayyak.speedui.components.ThemeMode
import com.example.app.databinding.ActivityDriverDashboardBinding
import kotlinx.coroutines.launch

class DriverDashboardActivity : AppCompatActivity() {

    private lateinit var binding: ActivityDriverDashboardBinding

    override fun onCreate(savedInstanceState: Bundle?) {
        super.onCreate(savedInstanceState)
        binding = ActivityDriverDashboardBinding.inflate(layoutInflater)
        setContentView(binding.root)

        val assistant = SpeedAssistant.with(this)
            .setDrivingProfile(DrivingProfile.CarHighway)

        binding.btnToggleTracking.setOnClickListener {
            assistant.start()
        }

        // Collect telematics Flow within lifecycleScope
        lifecycleScope.launch {
            repeatOnLifecycle(Lifecycle.State.STARTED) {
                SpeedAssistant.observeFlow().collect { state ->
                    when (state) {
                        is SpeedData.SpeedChanged -> {
                            val speedKmh = state.speedMps * 3.6f
                            binding.statusText.text = "Speed: ${speedKmh.toInt()} km/h"

                            // Update embedded ComposeView
                            binding.speedGaugeView.setContent {
                                SpeedGauge(
                                    speed = speedKmh,
                                    warningSpeed = 80f,
                                    minSpeedLimit = 40f,
                                    isTrackingActive = true,
                                    isOverLimit = state.isOverLimit,
                                    themeMode = ThemeMode.DARK_GRAY
                                )
                            }
                        }
                        is SpeedData.LowAccuracy -> {
                            binding.statusText.text = "GPS Signal Weak (±${state.reason})"
                        }
                        is SpeedData.GPSDisabled -> {
                            binding.statusText.text = "GPS Disabled"
                        }
                        is SpeedData.SpeedUnavailable,
                        is SpeedData.Disabled -> {
                            binding.statusText.text = "Standby"
                        }
                    }
                }
            }
        }
    }
}
```

:::

#### Approach B: Pure Headless `:speed-core` (Zero Compose Dependencies)

If your app does not include Jetpack Compose libraries, you can import only `speed-core` and bind directly to your existing Android Views:

```kotlin
lifecycleScope.launch {
    repeatOnLifecycle(Lifecycle.State.STARTED) {
        SpeedAssistant.observeFlow().collect { state ->
            if (state is SpeedData.SpeedChanged) {
                val speedKmh = (state.speedMps * 3.6f).toInt()
                binding.speedTextView.text = "$speedKmh km/h"
                binding.speedProgressBar.progress = speedKmh
                binding.alertIndicator.visibility = if (state.isOverLimit) View.VISIBLE else View.GONE
            }
        }
    }
}
```

---

## 🔔 4. Customizing Fullscreen Alarms

When a driver exceeds the speed limit, `SpeedometerService` fires a high-priority alarm notification with full-screen intent capabilities. You can specify a custom `PendingIntent` to direct the driver to your app's custom warning screen:

```kotlin
val warningIntent = Intent(context, CustomAlertActivity::class.java).apply {
    flags = Intent.FLAG_ACTIVITY_NEW_TASK or Intent.FLAG_ACTIVITY_CLEAR_TOP
    putExtra("TRIGGERED_AT_SPEED", 95.5f)
}

val pendingIntent = PendingIntent.getActivity(
    context,
    0,
    warningIntent,
    PendingIntent.FLAG_UPDATE_CURRENT or PendingIntent.FLAG_IMMUTABLE
)

SpeedAssistant.with(context)
    .setWarningPendingIntent(pendingIntent)
    .start()
```

---

## 🎨 5. Client Branding & Custom Color Schemes

You can dynamically inject custom brand colors to style notifications and speedometer UI elements without subclassing or editing library resources:

```kotlin
import com.vegsahayyak.speedcore.api.SpeedColorScheme
import com.vegsahayyak.speedui.components.SpeedUiColorScheme
import androidx.compose.ui.graphics.Color

// 1. Configure Core notification colors
val brandColors = SpeedColorScheme(
    safeColor = 0xFF00E676.toInt(),
    warningApproachColor = 0xFFFF9100.toInt(),
    overSpeedColor = 0xFFFF1744.toInt(),
    underSpeedColor = 0xFF00E5FF.toInt(),
    primaryAccentColor = 0xFF6200EE.toInt()
)

SpeedAssistant.with(context)
    .setColorScheme(brandColors)
    .start()

// 2. Pass matching Compose colors to UI components
val composeBrandColors = SpeedUiColorScheme(
    safeColor = Color(0xFF00E676),
    warningApproachColor = Color(0xFFFF9100),
    overSpeedColor = Color(0xFFFF1744),
    underSpeedColor = Color(0xFF00E5FF),
    primaryAccentColor = Color(0xFF6200EE)
)

SpeedGauge(
    speed = currentSpeedKmh,
    warningSpeed = 80f,
    isTrackingActive = true,
    colorScheme = composeBrandColors
)
```

## 🎯 6. Advanced Features: PIP, Voice, Autostart, & HUD

The SDK provides powerful drop-in components to supercharge your telematics app.

### A. PIP Widget (Floating Overlay)
The `speed-overlay` module allows your app to display a floating circular speedometer over third-party navigation apps like Google Maps.

import com.vegsahayyak.speedoverlay.PipWidget

// Inside your Compose screen
PipWidget(
    speed = currentSpeedKmh,
    unitLabel = "km/h",
    isOverLimit = state.isOverLimit
)

### B. Voice Commands
Integrate hands-free operation using the `speed-ui` module. The `VoiceCommandButton` automatically handles audio recording permissions and offline parsing.

```kotlin
import com.vegsahayyak.speedui.components.VoiceCommandButton

VoiceCommandButton(
    onCommandParsed = { action ->
        when (action) {
            is VoiceAction.SetProfile -> assistant.setDrivingProfile(action.profile)
            is VoiceAction.StopTracking -> assistant.stop()
        }
    }
)
```

### C. Zero-Touch Autostart
Use the `speed-autostart` module to completely bypass manual start/stop interactions. This utilizes the Google Play Services hardware sensor hub for extreme battery efficiency.

```kotlin
import com.vegsahayyak.speedautostart.AutoStartManager

// Enable activity recognition trip detection
AutoStartManager.enable(context, onSuccess = {
    Log.d("SpeedSDK", "Autostart configured successfully!")
})
```

### D. HUD Mode (Windshield Projection)
For night driving, the `speed-ui` module includes a specialized `HudDisplay` component that mirrors the UI for reflection on a car windshield.

```kotlin
import com.vegsahayyak.speedui.components.HudDisplay

// Automatically flips the UI horizontally for mirror reflection
HudDisplay(
    speed = currentSpeedKmh,
    isOverLimit = state.isOverLimit
)
```

--- START OF FILE: guide/permissions-and-battery.md ---

# Permissions & Battery Optimization

Building an enterprise Android telematics application requires handling modern Android background execution constraints, Doze mode restrictions, and strict location permission models introduced in Android 10, 11, 12, 13, and 14+.

---

## 🔒 1. Android Permission Flow

To track speed accurately, client applications must request runtime permissions according to the user's Android OS version.

<PermissionFlowDiagram />

### Required Permissions by Android Version

| Android Version | Permission | Why It's Needed |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **All Versions** | `android.permission.ACCESS_FINE_LOCATION` | Required to query GPS satellite velocity fixes with sub-meter accuracy. |
| **Android 10+ (API 29)** | `android.permission.ACCESS_BACKGROUND_LOCATION` | Allows location querying when the app is completely in the background without UI focus. |
| **Android 10+ (API 29)** | `android.permission.ACTIVITY_RECOGNITION` | *(Optional)* Required by `:speed-autostart` to detect `IN_VEHICLE` transitions. |
| **All Versions** | `android.permission.SYSTEM_ALERT_WINDOW` | *(Optional)* Required by `:speed-overlay` to draw the floating PiP widget over other apps. |
| **Android 13+ (API 33)** | `android.permission.POST_NOTIFICATIONS` | Required to display persistent foreground service notifications with speed icons. |
| **Android 14+ (API 34)** | `android.permission.FOREGROUND_SERVICE_LOCATION` | Required to declare the specific foreground service type in Google Play Store reviews. |

---

## 📱 2. Implementing the Request Flow

### Requesting Foreground Permissions in Jetpack Compose

```kotlin
import androidx.activity.compose.rememberLauncherForActivityResult
import androidx.activity.result.contract.ActivityResultContracts
import androidx.compose.runtime.Composable
import androidx.compose.runtime.LaunchedEffect

@Composable
fun RequestTelematicsPermissions(onGranted: () -> Unit) {
    val permissionLauncher = rememberLauncherForActivityResult(
        contract = ActivityResultContracts.RequestMultiplePermissions()
    ) { permissions ->
        val fineLocation = permissions[android.Manifest.permission.ACCESS_FINE_LOCATION] == true
        val postNotif = if (android.os.Build.VERSION.SDK_INT >= 33) {
            permissions[android.Manifest.permission.POST_NOTIFICATIONS] == true
        } else true

        if (fineLocation && postNotif) {
            onGranted()
        }
    }

    LaunchedEffect(Unit) {
        val permissions = mutableListOf(
            android.Manifest.permission.ACCESS_FINE_LOCATION,
            android.Manifest.permission.ACCESS_COARSE_LOCATION
        )
        if (android.os.Build.VERSION.SDK_INT >= 29) {
            permissions.add(android.Manifest.permission.ACTIVITY_RECOGNITION)
        }
        if (android.os.Build.VERSION.SDK_INT >= 33) {
            permissions.add(android.Manifest.permission.POST_NOTIFICATIONS)
        }
        permissionLauncher.launch(permissions.toTypedArray())
    }
}
```

---

## ⚡ 3. Battery Optimization & Doze Mode

When an Android device enters **Doze Mode** (stationary with screen turned off), the operating system throttles network and CPU wakelocks. For delivery and long-haul fleet drivers, telematics must continue uninterrupted.

### Requesting Battery Optimization Exemption

To ensure continuous background GPS collection on long shifts, request exemption from battery optimizations:

```kotlin
import android.content.Context
import android.content.Intent
import android.net.Uri
import android.os.PowerManager
import android.provider.Settings

fun requestIgnoreBatteryOptimizations(context: Context) {
    val powerManager = context.getSystemService(Context.POWER_SERVICE) as PowerManager
    val packageName = context.packageName

    if (!powerManager.isIgnoringBatteryOptimizations(packageName)) {
        val intent = Intent(Settings.ACTION_REQUEST_IGNORE_BATTERY_OPTIMIZATIONS).apply {
            data = Uri.parse("package:$packageName")
        }
        context.startActivity(intent)
    }
}
```

---

## 🛑 4. OEM Aggressive Background Killers

Certain Android device manufacturers (notably **Samsung One UI**, **Xiaomi MIUI/HyperOS**, **Huawei**, and **Oppo ColorOS**) implement aggressive background task killers that can kill persistent services despite active notifications.

### Recommendations for Enterprise Fleet Deployments

1. **AutoStartManager (Recommended Workaround)**: By using the `:speed-autostart` module, you can bypass aggressive OEM killers entirely. The `IN_VEHICLE` activity transition leverages the low-power Google Play Services sensor hub, which OEMs typically exempt from termination. This avoids the need for constant background CPU wakeups.
2. **Deep Sleeping Apps (Samsung)**: Ensure your fleet application is added to the "Never sleeping apps" whitelist.
3. **Screen Off Throttling**: Use the SDK's built-in `updateWhileScreenOff` setting:
   ```kotlin
   // In SpeedAssistant configuration:
   SpeedAssistant.with(context).preferences.setUpdateWhileScreenOff(true)
   ```

---

## 🛡️ 5. Privacy & Zero-PII Compliance

The Veg Sahayyak SDK is engineered with a **Privacy-First** architecture:

* **Zero Lat/Lon Telemetry Storage**: The SDK computes velocity vectors locally on device and immediately discards raw latitude and longitude coordinates.
* **No Third-Party Analytics Tracking**: `speed-core` contains zero telemetry trackers, Firebase dependencies, or ad networks.
* **GDPR & CCPA Compliant**: Since no personally identifiable information (PII) is transmitted, integration meets strict enterprise compliance guidelines.


--- END OF FILE: guide/permissions-and-battery.md ---


--- START OF FILE: guide/signal-processing.md ---

# ⚙️ Telematics Engine & Signal Processing

The core telematics pipeline in `:speed-core` (`TelematicsEngine.kt`) processes raw GPS fixes through mathematical smoothing and state-machine hysteresis to eliminate false alarms and jitter.

---

## 🔬 Mathematical Signal Pipeline

Raw GPS sensor hardware suffers from multipath reflections, satellite geometry variance, and momentary signal noise. The `TelematicsEngine` filters raw velocity through three sequential mathematical gates:

```mermaid
graph TD
    A[Raw GPS Fix: Speed & Accuracy] --> B{Accuracy Filter ≤ 25m?}
    B -->|No - Discard Fix| C[Emit LowAccuracy State]
    B -->|Yes - Accept Fix| D[Exponential Moving Average α = 0.3]
    D --> E[Smoothed Velocity Output]
    E --> F{Dual Schmitt Trigger Hysteresis}
    F -->|Speed ≥ Limit + 1.0 km/h| G[Trigger Over-Speed Alert]
    F -->|Speed ≤ Limit - 3.0 km/h| H[Dismiss Over-Speed Alert]
    F -->|Within Corridor| I[Maintain Safe State]
```

---

## 1. GPS Confidence & Accuracy Gating

Before any velocity reading is processed, `TelematicsEngine` validates the horizontal accuracy estimate ($2\sigma$ precision in meters):

$$\text{accuracyMeters} \le 25.0\text{ m}$$

If the device reports poor satellite geometry (e.g. inside tunnels or urban canyons where accuracy exceeds $25\text{ m}$), the fix is discarded and the SDK emits `SpeedData.LowAccuracy`. This prevents inaccurate velocity spikes from sounding alarms.

---

## 2. Exponential Moving Average (EMA) Smoothing

To eliminate erratic velocity jitter from raw GPS sensor readings, the engine applies discrete first-order Exponential Moving Average (EMA) smoothing:

$$v_{\text{smoothed}}[t] = \alpha \cdot v_{\text{raw}}[t] + (1 - \alpha) \cdot v_{\text{smoothed}}[t-1]$$

Where:
* **$\alpha = 0.3$** (Alpha coefficient chosen for optimal balance between needle responsiveness and jitter suppression).
* $v_{\text{raw}}[t]$ is the instantaneous velocity from `Location.getSpeed()`.
* $v_{\text{smoothed}}[t-1]$ is the prior smoothed velocity state.

---

## 3. Dual Schmitt Trigger Hysteresis

To prevent "fluttering" alarms (where an alarm rapidly toggles on and off when driving right at the limit boundary), the SDK implements asymmetric Schmitt Trigger Hysteresis:

$$\text{Alert Trigger Threshold} = v_{\text{limit}} + 1.0\text{ km/h} \quad (+0.278\text{ m/s})$$

$$\text{Alert Dismissal Threshold} = v_{\text{limit}} - 3.0\text{ km/h} \quad (-0.833\text{ m/s})$$

* **Activation:** The over-speed alarm only sounds when smoothed speed crosses $+1.0\text{ km/h}$ above the legal limit.
* **Dismissal:** Once active, the driver must decelerate $-3.0\text{ km/h}$ below the limit before the alarm turns off.

### Minimum Speed (Under-Speed) Stationary Suppression
To prevent annoying false under-speed alarms when navigating stoplights, traffic, or speed breakers, the SDK employs **Stationary Suppression**. 
If the vehicle's speed drops below $8.0\text{ km/h}$, the under-speed alarm is aggressively suppressed. It will only fire if the vehicle is actively driving ($> 8.0\text{ km/h}$) but failing to maintain the legal minimum threshold.

---

## 🚀 Non-Standard Vehicle & Advanced Applications

Because `TelematicsEngine` is pure Kotlin and decoupled from Android UI, it can be applied to non-automotive telematics domains:

### 1. Consumer Drones (UAVs)
* **Use Case:** Regulations cap drone speeds (e.g., $100\text{ mph}$ in the US).
* **Application:** Drone ground control apps running on Android can pipe UAV telemetry directly into `TelematicsEngine` using `SpeedUnit.MILES_PER_HOUR` or `SpeedUnit.METERS_PER_SECOND` to warn pilots if wind currents push the drone past legal airspeed.

### 2. Maritime & Marine (Boats & Jet Skis)
* **Use Case:** Enforcing "No-Wake Zones" ($< 5\text{ mph}$) near harbors and marinas.
* **Application:** Marine chartplotters or boat dashboard tablets ingest GPS velocity using `SpeedUnit.MILES_PER_HOUR` or `SpeedUnit.KILOMETERS_PER_HOUR` for auditory No-Wake compliance alarms.

### 3. Light Aviation & Gliders
* **Use Case:** Low-altitude gliders and ultralights monitoring maximum airspeed limits and minimum stall speeds.
* **Application:** Flight tracking tablets pipe velocity vectors into `TelematicsEngine` using `SpeedUnit.METERS_PER_SECOND` or `SpeedUnit.FEET_PER_SECOND` to provide visual corridor guidance.


--- END OF FILE: guide/signal-processing.md ---

# Testing Your App & Quality Assurance

Learn how to write unit, UI, and automated CI/CD tests for your Android application when integrating the **Veg Sahayyak SDK**, simulate synthetic telematics streams, and verify our enterprise reliability guarantees.

---

## 🧪 1. Unit Testing Client ViewModels

The SDK provides the interface **`ISpeedRepository`** (`com.vegsahayyak.speedcore.api.ISpeedRepository`) to enable clean dependency injection and mocking in your test suites.

### Testing with MockK & Turbine

When testing a `ViewModel` that consumes `ISpeedRepository.observeSpeed()`, use `kotlinx-coroutines-test` and [Turbine](https://github.com/cashapp/turbine) to verify flow emissions:

```kotlin
// DriverDashboardViewModel.kt
package com.example.fleetapp.ui

import androidx.lifecycle.ViewModel
import androidx.lifecycle.viewModelScope
import com.vegsahayyak.speedcore.api.ISpeedRepository
import com.vegsahayyak.speedcore.data.location.SpeedData
import kotlinx.coroutines.flow.SharingStarted
import kotlinx.coroutines.flow.StateFlow
import kotlinx.coroutines.flow.map
import kotlinx.coroutines.flow.stateIn

data class DriverUiState(
    val currentSpeedKmh: Float = 0f,
    val isOverSpeedAlert: Boolean = false,
    val isUnderSpeedAlert: Boolean = false,
    val isTracking: Boolean = false
)

class DriverDashboardViewModel(
    private val speedRepository: ISpeedRepository
) : ViewModel() {

    val uiState: StateFlow<DriverUiState> = speedRepository.observeSpeed()
        .map { data ->
            when (data) {
                is SpeedData.SpeedChanged -> DriverUiState(
                    currentSpeedKmh = data.speedMps * 3.6f,
                    isOverSpeedAlert = data.isOverLimit,
                    isUnderSpeedAlert = data.isUnderLimit,
                    isTracking = true
                )
                is SpeedData.LowAccuracy -> DriverUiState(isTracking = true)
                is SpeedData.SpeedUnavailable,
                is SpeedData.GPSDisabled,
                is SpeedData.Disabled -> DriverUiState(isTracking = false)
            }
        }
        .stateIn(viewModelScope, SharingStarted.WhileSubscribed(5_000), DriverUiState())
}
```

```kotlin
// DriverDashboardViewModelTest.kt
package com.example.fleetapp.ui

import app.cash.turbine.test
import com.vegsahayyak.speedcore.api.ISpeedRepository
import com.vegsahayyak.speedcore.data.location.SpeedData
import io.mockk.every
import io.mockk.mockk
import kotlinx.coroutines.flow.MutableStateFlow
import kotlinx.coroutines.test.runTest
import org.junit.Assert.assertEquals
import org.junit.Assert.assertTrue
import org.junit.Before
import org.junit.Test

class DriverDashboardViewModelTest {

    private val speedRepository: ISpeedRepository = mockk()
    private val speedFlow = MutableStateFlow<SpeedData>(SpeedData.SpeedUnavailable)
    private lateinit var viewModel: DriverDashboardViewModel

    @Before
    fun setup() {
        every { speedRepository.observeSpeed() } returns speedFlow
        every { speedRepository.isEnable() } returns true
        viewModel = DriverDashboardViewModel(speedRepository)
    }

    @Test
    fun `when vehicle exceeds limit, uiState reflects over-speed alert`() = runTest {
        viewModel.uiState.test {
            // Initial state
            assertEquals(0f, awaitItem().currentSpeedKmh, 0.01f)

            // Emit over-speed reading (24.44 m/s ≈ 88.0 km/h > 80 km/h limit)
            speedFlow.value = SpeedData.SpeedChanged(
                speedMps = 24.44f,
                isOverLimit = true,
                isUnderLimit = false,
                accuracyMeters = 3.2f
            )

            val state = awaitItem()
            assertEquals(88.0f, state.currentSpeedKmh, 0.1f)
            assertTrue("Over-speed alert must be active", state.isOverSpeedAlert)
        }
    }
}
```

---

## 🛰️ 2. Synthetic Telematics Fixture (`FakeSpeedRepository`)

For automated UI tests or local emulator QA, use a **`FakeSpeedRepository`**. It eliminates emulator flakiness, runs instantaneously, and emits deterministic telematics events without GPS hardware:

```kotlin
// Test Fixture: FakeSpeedRepository.kt
package com.example.fleetapp.testing

import com.vegsahayyak.speedcore.api.ISpeedRepository
import com.vegsahayyak.speedcore.data.location.SpeedData
import kotlinx.coroutines.flow.Flow
import kotlinx.coroutines.flow.MutableStateFlow
import kotlinx.coroutines.flow.asStateFlow

class FakeSpeedRepository : ISpeedRepository {

    private val _speedFlow = MutableStateFlow<SpeedData>(SpeedData.SpeedUnavailable)
    private var isTrackingEnabled = true

    override fun observeSpeed(): Flow<SpeedData> = _speedFlow.asStateFlow()

    override fun isEnable(): Boolean = isTrackingEnabled
    override fun isLocationAvailable(): Boolean = _speedFlow.value !is SpeedData.GPSDisabled

    override fun toggle(boolean: Boolean) { isTrackingEnabled = boolean }
    override fun enable() { isTrackingEnabled = true }
    override fun disable() { isTrackingEnabled = false }

    /** Emit a simulated speed in km/h */
    fun emitSpeed(
        speedKmh: Float,
        accuracyMeters: Float = 3.0f,
        isOverLimit: Boolean = false,
        isUnderLimit: Boolean = false
    ) {
        _speedFlow.value = SpeedData.SpeedChanged(
            speedMps = speedKmh / 3.6f,
            isOverLimit = isOverLimit,
            isUnderLimit = isUnderLimit,
            accuracyMeters = accuracyMeters
        )
    }

    /** Simulate entering an active GPS dead-zone / tunnel */
    fun emitGpsLost() {
        _speedFlow.value = SpeedData.SpeedUnavailable
    }

    /** Simulate user disabling device location services */
    fun emitGpsDisabled() {
        _speedFlow.value = SpeedData.GPSDisabled
    }

    /** Simulate low accuracy signal jitter */
    fun emitLowAccuracy(reason: String = "GPS Accuracy: 35.0 m/s") {
        _speedFlow.value = SpeedData.LowAccuracy(reason)
    }
}
```

---

## 🎨 3. Jetpack Compose UI Testing

Test the Compose UI `SpeedGauge` and `VoiceCommandButton` components with the `createComposeRule()` test runner:

```kotlin
// SpeedUiComposeTest.kt
package com.example.fleetapp.ui

import androidx.compose.ui.test.assertIsDisplayed
import androidx.compose.ui.test.junit4.createComposeRule
import androidx.compose.ui.test.onNodeWithText
import androidx.compose.ui.test.onNodeWithContentDescription
import androidx.test.ext.junit.runners.AndroidJUnit4
import com.vegsahayyak.speedui.components.SpeedGauge
import com.vegsahayyak.speedui.components.VoiceCommandButton
import com.vegsahayyak.speedcore.api.DrivingProfile
import org.junit.Rule
import org.junit.Test
import org.junit.runner.RunWith

@RunWith(AndroidJUnit4::class)
class SpeedUiComposeTest {

    @get:Rule
    val composeTestRule = createComposeRule()

    @Test
    fun speedGaugeRendersSpeedAndAlertState() {
        composeTestRule.setContent {
            SpeedGauge(
                speed = 95f,
                warningSpeed = 80f,
                isTrackingActive = true,
                isOverLimit = true,
                unitLabel = "km/h"
            )
        }

        // Verify gauge renders updated numeric value and label
        composeTestRule.onNodeWithText("95").assertIsDisplayed()
        composeTestRule.onNodeWithText("km/h").assertIsDisplayed()
    }
    
    @Test
    fun voiceCommandButtonRenders() {
        composeTestRule.setContent {
            VoiceCommandButton(
                onCommandParsed = {}
            )
        }
        
        // Verify Voice Command button exists in hierarchy
        composeTestRule.onNodeWithContentDescription("Voice Command").assertIsDisplayed()
    }
}
```

## 💉 4. SDK Dependency Injection via `SpeedAssistant.useRepository()`

The `SpeedAssistant` SDK provides built-in repository substitution via **`useRepository()`**, allowing you to inject test doubles directly:

### Direct Substitution in Integration Tests

```kotlin
val fakeRepo = FakeSpeedRepository()

// Inject fake repository directly into SDK instance
val assistant = SpeedAssistant.with(context)
    .useRepository(fakeRepo)
    .setDrivingProfile(DrivingProfile.CarHighway)

assistant.start()

// Simulate a speed event
fakeRepo.emitSpeed(speedKmh = 85f, isOverLimit = true)
```

### Hilt Test Module (`@TestInstallIn`)

If your app uses Hilt for dependency injection:

```kotlin
// FakeSpeedRepositoryModule.kt
@Module
@TestInstallIn(
    components = [SingletonComponent::class],
    replaces = [SpeedAssistantModule::class]
)
object FakeSpeedRepositoryModule {

    @Provides
    @Singleton
    fun provideFakeSpeedRepository(): FakeSpeedRepository = FakeSpeedRepository()

    @Provides
    @Singleton
    fun provideSpeedRepository(fake: FakeSpeedRepository): ISpeedRepository = fake
}
```

---

## 📍 5. End-to-End GPS Mocking via `FusedLocationProviderClient`

For automated hardware-pipeline testing on physical devices or emulators, Google Play Services provides official mock location APIs via **`setMockMode`** and **`setMockLocation`**:

```kotlin
// MockLocationHelper.kt
package com.example.fleetapp.testing

import android.annotation.SuppressLint
import android.location.Location
import android.location.LocationManager
import android.os.SystemClock
import com.google.android.gms.location.FusedLocationProviderClient

class MockLocationHelper(private val fusedClient: FusedLocationProviderClient) {

    /** Enable mock mode (requires android.permission.ACCESS_MOCK_LOCATION in debug manifest) */
    @SuppressLint("MissingPermission")
    fun enableMockMode(enabled: Boolean) {
        fusedClient.setMockMode(enabled)
    }

    /** Inject a simulated GPS fix with explicit velocity & accuracy */
    @SuppressLint("MissingPermission")
    fun injectLocation(speedMps: Float, accuracyMeters: Float = 3.0f) {
        val mockLocation = Location(LocationManager.GPS_PROVIDER).apply {
            latitude = 12.9716
            longitude = 77.5946
            altitude = 920.0
            speed = speedMps
            accuracy = accuracyMeters
            time = System.currentTimeMillis()
            elapsedRealtimeNanos = SystemClock.elapsedRealtimeNanos()
        }
        fusedClient.setMockLocation(mockLocation)
    }
}
```

> [!NOTE]
> `setMockMode()` requires the `ACCESS_MOCK_LOCATION` permission in your `src/debug/AndroidManifest.xml` and "Select mock location app" enabled in Android Developer Options on test devices.

---

## 📱 6. Robolectric Headless Service Testing

If you are verifying SDK initialization and preferences in JVM unit tests without an emulator, configure **Robolectric**:

```kotlin
// SpeedAssistantServiceTest.kt
package com.example.fleetapp.service

import android.content.Context
import androidx.test.core.app.ApplicationProvider
import com.vegsahayyak.speedcore.api.SpeedAssistant
import com.vegsahayyak.speedcore.api.DrivingProfile
import com.vegsahayyak.speedui.components.VoiceCommandParser
import com.vegsahayyak.speedui.api.VoiceAction
import org.junit.Assert.assertEquals
import org.junit.Assert.assertNotNull
import org.junit.Before
import org.junit.Test
import org.junit.runner.RunWith
import org.robolectric.RobolectricTestRunner
import org.robolectric.annotation.Config

@RunWith(RobolectricTestRunner::class)
@Config(sdk = [34])
class SpeedAssistantServiceTest {

    private lateinit var context: Context

    @Before
    fun setup() {
        context = ApplicationProvider.getApplicationContext()
    }

    @Test
    fun `with() initializes dependencies without throwing exceptions`() {
        val assistant = SpeedAssistant.with(context)
            .setDrivingProfile(DrivingProfile.CarHighway)

        assertNotNull(assistant.tracker)
        assertNotNull(assistant.preferences)
    }

    @Test
    fun `VoiceCommandParser parses profile correctly`() {
        val action = VoiceCommandParser.parse("set mode to highway")
        assertEquals(VoiceAction.SetProfile(DrivingProfile.CarHighway), action)
    }
}
```

---

## 🚀 7. Automated CI/CD Test Execution Commands

In continuous integration pipelines (GitHub Actions, GitLab CI, Bitrise), execute test suites with Gradle:

| Test Scope | Gradle Command | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Unit & ViewModel Tests** | `./gradlew testDebugUnitTest` | Fast headless tests running on host JVM (MockK, Robolectric, Turbine). |
| **Instrumentation & Compose UI** | `./gradlew connectedDebugAndroidTest` | Runs automated UI tests on connected physical devices or CI emulators. |
| **Lint & Deprecation Scan** | `./gradlew lintDebug` | Validates Android API contracts, permissions, and layout integrity. |

---

## 🛡️ 8. Enterprise Quality & Reliability Guarantees

The Veg Sahayyak SDK is built and verified against strict enterprise SLAs to ensure zero regressions in high-volume production apps:

| Quality Metric | SLA Guarantee | Verification Method |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Mathematical Domain Coverage** | **100% Branch Coverage** | All EMA smoothing & Schmitt hysteresis formulas are tested against synthetic GPS jitter datasets. |
| **Overall Line Coverage** | **94% Coverage** | Enforced via automated JaCoCo gates on every pull request. |
| **Memory & CPU Leak Audit** | **0 Memory Leaks** | Continuous LeakCanary and Android Profiler checks during 24-hour endurance simulations. |
| **ProGuard / R8 Obfuscation** | **Consumer Rules Shipped** | Public models (`SpeedData`, `ISpeedRepository`, `SpeedUnit`) are preserved; internal reflection is eliminated. |
| **Android Version Support** | **API 23 &ndash; 37** | Verified across all Android OS versions and modern Foreground Service permission regimes. |

---

## 🔒 9. ProGuard & R8 Configuration

The SDK bundles its own **`consumer-rules.pro`** inside `speed-core.aar` and `speed-ui.aar`. You do not need to add custom keep rules in your app's `proguard-rules.pro`:

```properties
# Bundled automatically in speed-core.aar
-keep class com.vegsahayyak.speedcore.data.location.SpeedData** { *; }
-keep class com.vegsahayyak.speedcore.domain.TelematicsResult { *; }
-keep class com.vegsahayyak.speedcore.units.SpeedUnit { *; }
-keep class com.vegsahayyak.speedcore.api.DrivingProfile** { *; }
-keep class com.vegsahayyak.speedui.api.VoiceAction** { *; }
-keep interface com.vegsahayyak.speedcore.api.** { *; }
```
