--- START OF FILE: guide/voice-commands.md ---

# 🎙️ Hands-Free Voice Commands & AI NLU

The `:speed-ui` module provides a drop-in **Voice Command System** enabling commercial drivers, couriers, and motorists to adjust speed thresholds hands-free without looking away from the road.

---

## 🎯 Architectural Overview

The Voice Command pipeline is divided into two distinct responsibilities:
1. **Speech-to-Text Layer (`VoiceCommandButton`)**: Listens to microphone audio via Android's native `SpeechRecognizer` Activity Contract and transcribes voice into text.
2. **Intent Parsing Layer (`VoiceCommandParser`)**: Translates raw text strings into structured `VoiceAction` domain events (offline Regex or remote LLM).

```mermaid
graph TD
    A[Driver Spoken Audio] --> B[VoiceCommandButton Composable]
    B -->|Transcribed Text| C{VoiceCommandParser}
    C -->|Offline Regex| D[RegexVoiceCommandParser]
    C -->|Cloud LLM| E[GeminiVoiceParser]
    D --> F[VoiceAction.SetMaxLimit / SetMinLimit / ChangeUnit]
    E --> F
    F --> G[SpeedAssistant.with context .setWarningSpeedThreshold]
```

---

## 📦 Basic Usage (`VoiceCommandButton`)

Drop the `VoiceCommandButton` into your Compose dashboard:

```kotlin
import androidx.compose.runtime.Composable
import androidx.compose.ui.Modifier
import com.vegsahayyak.speedui.components.VoiceCommandButton
import com.vegsahayyak.speedui.api.VoiceAction
import com.vegsahayyak.speedcore.api.SpeedAssistant

@Composable
fun DriverDashboard() {
    VoiceCommandButton(
        onActionParsed = { action ->
            when (action) {
                is VoiceAction.SetMaxLimit -> {
                    // Spoken: "Set limit to 80"
                    SpeedAssistant.with(context).setWarningSpeedThreshold(action.limit)
                }
                is VoiceAction.SetMinLimit -> {
                    // Spoken: "Set minimum speed to 40"
                    SpeedAssistant.with(context).setMinWarningSpeedThreshold(action.limit)
                }
                is VoiceAction.ChangeUnit -> {
                    // Spoken: "Change unit to miles per hour"
                    println("Switching unit to ${action.unitName}")
                }
                is VoiceAction.Unknown -> {
                    println("Voice command not recognized")
                }
            }
        }
    )
}
```

---

## 🌐 Multilingual Regex Parsing (`RegexVoiceCommandParser`)

By default, the SDK uses `RegexVoiceCommandParser` which operates **100% offline with zero network latency**. You can configure custom regex patterns to support non-English international markets:

```kotlin
import com.vegsahayyak.speedui.utils.RegexVoiceCommandParser

val multilingualParser = RegexVoiceCommandParser()

// In your Compose hierarchy:
VoiceCommandButton(
    parser = multilingualParser,
    onActionParsed = { action -> /* handle action */ }
)
```

### Supported Default Commands (English)
* *"Set max speed to 80"* $\rightarrow$ `VoiceAction.SetMaxLimit(80f)`
* *"Speed limit 100"* $\rightarrow$ `VoiceAction.SetMaxLimit(100f)`
* *"Set minimum speed to 40"* $\rightarrow$ `VoiceAction.SetMinLimit(40f)`
* *"Switch to miles per hour"* $\rightarrow$ `VoiceAction.ChangeUnit("MILES_PER_HOUR")`
* *"Change unit to kilometers"* $\rightarrow$ `VoiceAction.ChangeUnit("KILOMETERS_PER_HOUR")`

---

## 🤖 Advanced AI / Google Gemini NLU Integration

For enterprise fleets requiring natural language understanding (e.g. interpreting *"Hey assistant, please cap my speed at seventy-five miles an hour"* or handling regional dialects), implement the `VoiceCommandParser` interface and connect to Google Gemini:

```kotlin
import com.vegsahayyak.speedui.api.VoiceCommandParser
import com.vegsahayyak.speedui.api.VoiceAction
import com.google.ai.client.generativeai.GenerativeModel

class GeminiVoiceCommandParser(
    private val generativeModel: GenerativeModel
) : VoiceCommandParser {

    override suspend fun parse(text: String): VoiceAction? {
        val prompt = """
            You are an in-vehicle telematics assistant. The driver said: "$text".
            Extract their intent into JSON:
            - If setting max limit: {"action": "SET_MAX", "limit": 80}
            - If setting min limit: {"action": "SET_MIN", "limit": 40}
            - If changing unit: {"action": "CHANGE_UNIT", "unit": "km/h"}
            Return only raw JSON.
        """.trimIndent()

        val response = generativeModel.generateContent(prompt)
        val rawJson = response.text ?: return VoiceAction.Unknown

        return parseJsonResponse(rawJson)
    }

    private fun parseJsonResponse(json: String): VoiceAction {
        // Parse JSON into VoiceAction instances
        return VoiceAction.SetMaxLimit(80f)
    }
}
```

Inject your custom AI parser into `VoiceCommandButton`:

```kotlin
VoiceCommandButton(
    parser = GeminiVoiceCommandParser(myGeminiModel),
    onActionParsed = { action -> /* handle action */ }
)
```

---

## 🛡️ Required Android Permissions

The `VoiceCommandButton` automatically handles launching the Android speech intent. Ensure `RECORD_AUDIO` is declared in your app's `AndroidManifest.xml`:

```xml
<uses-permission android:name="android.permission.RECORD_AUDIO" />
```

## 🚀 Quick Integration in 3 Steps

::: code-group

```kotlin [1. Add Repository (settings.gradle.kts)]
dependencyResolutionManagement {
    repositories {
        google()
        mavenCentral()
        
        // Authenticate with GitHub Packages
        maven {
            name = "VegSahayyakSDK"
            url = uri("https://maven.pkg.github.com/VegSahayyak/veg-sahayyak-sdk")
            credentials {
                username = "YOUR_GITHUB_USERNAME"
                password = "YOUR_READ_ONLY_PAT"
            }
        }
    }
}
```

```kotlin [2. Add Dependencies (app/build.gradle.kts)]
dependencies {
    // 1. Bill of Materials for version alignment
    implementation(platform("com.vegsahayyak:speed-bom:2.1.0"))
    
    // 2. Headless tracking & alarm logic
    implementation("com.vegsahayyak:speed-core")
    
    // 3. Optional Jetpack Compose Speedometer & HUD UI
    implementation("com.vegsahayyak:speed-ui")

    // 4. Optional PiP floating overlay & Activity Recognition plugins
    implementation("com.vegsahayyak:speed-overlay")
    implementation("com.vegsahayyak:speed-autostart")
}
```

```kotlin [3. Initialize & Start (MainActivity.kt)]
class MainActivity : ComponentActivity() {
    override fun onCreate(savedInstanceState: Bundle?) {
        super.onCreate(savedInstanceState)
        
        // 1. Configure and launch headless tracking
        val assistant = SpeedAssistant.with(this)
            .setWarningSpeedThreshold(80f) // Alert threshold in km/h
            .setMinWarningSpeedThreshold(40f) // Minimum corridor threshold

        assistant.start()

        // 2. Render Jetpack Compose UI
        setContent {
            val speedState by SpeedAssistant.observeFlow().collectAsState(initial = SpeedData.SpeedUnavailable)
            val currentSpeedKmh = (speedState as? SpeedData.SpeedChanged)?.let { it.speedMps * 3.6f } ?: 0f
            val isOverLimit = (speedState as? SpeedData.SpeedChanged)?.isOverLimit ?: false
            
            SpeedGauge(
                speed = currentSpeedKmh,
                warningSpeed = 80f,
                isTrackingActive = true,
                isOverLimit = isOverLimit,
                unitLabel = "km/h"
            )
        }
    }
}
```

:::

## 🌟 Overview & Reference Role

The **Speed Assistant App** serves as the primary **production reference implementation** of the `Veg Sahayyak SDK` (`com.vegsahayyak:speed-core` and `com.vegsahayyak:speed-ui`).

Instead of maintaining a separate in-house telematics pipeline, the Speed Assistant consumer app delegates all GPS velocity calculation, signal noise filtering, threshold monitoring, and speedometer gauge rendering directly to the SDK.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    subgraph "Speed Assistant Consumer App"
        UI[App Navigation & Settings]
        Audio[Audio / Haptic Engine]
    end

    subgraph "Veg Sahayyak SDK"
        Core["com.vegsahayyak:speed-core\n(EMA Filter + Schmitt Trigger + Fused Location)"]
        ComposeUI["com.vegsahayyak:speed-ui\n(@Composable SpeedGauge)"]
    end

    subgraph "Android OS Hardware"
        GPS[(Fused Location Provider)]
        Screen[(Hardware Canvas / GPU)]
    end

    GPS --> Core
    Core --> UI
    Core --> Audio
    Core --> ComposeUI
    ComposeUI --> Screen
```

---

## ⚡ Technical Benchmarks in Production

| Dimension | Engineering Guarantee | SDK Implementation |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Memory Footprint** | **`< 5 MB` runtime heap** | Headless core engine with zero memory leaks and minimal object allocations in the critical location loop. |
| **UI Render Performance** | **Fluid `60 FPS`** | Hardware-accelerated Canvas rendering via `@Composable SpeedGauge`. |
| **GPS Velocity Smoothing** | **Real-time `α = 0.3` EMA** | Eliminates raw sensor jitter without introducing perceptible lag. |
| **Threshold Stability** | **Dual Schmitt Hysteresis** | `+1.0 km/h` upper trigger / `-3.0 km/h` reset threshold eliminates alarm flutter. |
| **Lifecycle Compliance** | **Android 10 to 15+ Safe** | Native `FOREGROUND_SERVICE_LOCATION` handling with zero unneeded wake-locks when stationary. |

---

## 🛠️ How the Production App Implements the SDK

The reference application integrates the SDK using standard Kotlin Coroutines and Jetpack Compose state collection:

### 1. Initialization in Application / Activity
```kotlin
// Initialize and configure headless telematics
val speedAssistant = SpeedAssistant.with(context)
    .setWarningSpeedThreshold(80f)      // Alert threshold in km/h
    .setMinWarningSpeedThreshold(30f)   // Minimum corridor threshold
    .setColorScheme(
        SpeedColorScheme(
            safeColor = 0xFF00E676.toInt(),
            overSpeedColor = 0xFFFF1744.toInt(),
            underSpeedColor = 0xFF00E5FF.toInt()
        )
    )

// Start headless foreground service
speedAssistant.start()
```

### 2. Rendering the HUD Gauge in Jetpack Compose
```kotlin
@Composable
fun DriverDashboardScreen() {
    val speedState by SpeedAssistant.observeFlow()
        .collectAsState(initial = SpeedData.SpeedUnavailable)

    val currentSpeedKmh = (speedState as? SpeedData.SpeedChanged)?.let { 
        it.speedMps * 3.6f 
    } ?: 0f

    val isOverLimit = (speedState as? SpeedData.SpeedChanged)?.isOverLimit ?: false

    Column(
        modifier = Modifier
            .fillMaxSize()
            .background(Color.Black),
        horizontalAlignment = Alignment.CenterHorizontally,
        verticalArrangement = Arrangement.Center
    ) {
        SpeedGauge(
            speed = currentSpeedKmh,
            warningSpeed = 80f,
            minSpeedLimit = 30f,
            isTrackingActive = true,
            isOverLimit = isOverLimit,
            unitLabel = "km/h",
            themeMode = ThemeMode.OLED_BLACK
        )
    }
}
```

--- START OF FILE: standards/01_ARCHITECTURE_AND_CODE_STANDARDS.md ---

# Architecture & Code Standards

These guidelines define the structural rules and engineering standards for the **Veg Sahayyak SDK** codebase. AI agents and developers must adhere to these standards to maintain a clean, testable, and scalable modular architecture.

---

## 1. Modular Architecture Boundaries

The repository is organized into distinct Gradle modules with strict boundaries:

- **`:speed-core` (Headless Telematics Engine)**
  - **Responsibility:** Mathematical signal processing (`TelematicsEngine`), Fused Location polling (`SpeedWatcher`), `SpeedColorScheme`, and foreground service lifecycle (`SpeedometerService`).
  - **Rules:** **CRITICAL:** Jetpack Compose dependencies (e.g., `androidx.compose.ui`) must **never** leak into `:speed-core`. Minimal third-party footprint (only Google Play Services Location and Coroutines). Does not force DI frameworks on consuming clients.
- **`:speed-ui` (Jetpack Compose Visual Layer)**
  - **Responsibility:** Hardware-accelerated canvas speedometer (`SpeedGauge`), HUD digital display (`HudDisplay`), windshield reflection modifiers (`Modifier.hudMirror`), accessibility semantics, and automotive themes (`SpeedUiColorScheme`).
  - **Rules:** Depends on `:speed-core` and Jetpack Compose. No direct Android framework storage or location polling.
- **`:speed-overlay` (Floating PiP Overlay Widget)**
  - **Responsibility:** Lightweight floating Picture-in-Picture window (`PipWidget`) for persistent speed display over third-party navigation apps.
  - **Rules:** Optional plugin module. Decoupled from core logic.
- **`:speed-autostart` (Zero-Touch Autostart Plugin)**
  - **Responsibility:** Background trip detection (`AutoStartManager`) via Google Play Activity Recognition (`IN_VEHICLE` transitions).
  - **Rules:** Optional plugin module. Zero runtime overhead for clients not needing automatic drive detection.
- **`:speed-bom` (Bill of Materials)**
  - **Responsibility:** Gradle platform artifact enforcing version alignment across SDK modules.
- **`:app` (Sample / Demo Application)**
  - **Responsibility:** End-to-end integration demo showing `SpeedAssistant` usage in real-world Activity, Compose, and Hilt environments.

---

## 2. Dependency Injection Strategy

- **SDK Modules (`:speed-core`, `:speed-ui`)**:
  - Employs a lightweight internal service locator (`SpeedCoreInternal`) to avoid imposing heavy DI frameworks on consuming clients.
  - Public interfaces (`ISpeedRepository`, `IPreferenceRepository`) can be overridden at runtime via `SpeedAssistant.useRepository()` or `SpeedAssistant.usePreferenceRepository()`.
- **Sample App (`:app`)**:
  - Hilt is used for sample app dependency injection.
  - Test modules use `@TestInstallIn` to bind test doubles (e.g. `FakeSpeedRepository`).

---

## 3. UI Framework: Jetpack Compose

- **New Features:** All new UI must be written in **Jetpack Compose**.
- **Canvas Rendering:** Automotive gauges must use hardware-accelerated Compose Canvas drawing with precomputed trigonometric lookup tables and tokens.
- **State Hoisting:** UIs should be stateless. Hoist state to callers using `StateFlow<SpeedData>`.
- **Naming:** Composable functions must be PascalCase and annotated with `@Composable` (e.g., `SpeedGauge`, `GaugeNeedle`).

---

## 4. State Management & Concurrency

- Use **Kotlin Coroutines** and **Flows**.
- Expose state streams using `Flow<SpeedData>` or `StateFlow`.
- Thread boundary rules:
  - Location event handling and mathematical filtering run on `Dispatchers.Default`.
  - Service lifecycle and notification updates run on `Dispatchers.Main.immediate`.

---

## 5. Coding Conventions

- **Language:** Kotlin only (Kotlin 1.9+ / 2.0+).
- **Formatting:** Adhere to standard ktlint and detekt guidelines.
- **Null Safety:** Avoid `!!` (not-null assertions). Use safe calls (`?.`) or Elvis operators (`?:`).
- **Data Classes:** Use `data class` for immutable state models (`SpeedData.SpeedChanged`, `TelematicsResult`).
- **Early-Exits (Guard Clauses):** Return early in validation logic instead of deeply nesting code inside `if` statements.
- **DRY & KISS:** Extract repeated mathematical conversions into `SpeedUnit` and domain extensions.
- **Meaningful KDoc:** Document mathematical constants (e.g., alpha EMA factor, Schmitt trigger delta values) and unit expectations on all public APIs.


--- END OF FILE: standards/01_ARCHITECTURE_AND_CODE_STANDARDS.md ---


--- START OF FILE: standards/02_FEATURE_DEVELOPMENT_WORKFLOW.md ---

# Feature Development Workflow

This document outlines the standard operating procedure for adding new features to the project. AI agents must follow this pipeline sequentially.

## 1. Requirement & Planning Phase
- **Understand the Goal:** Cross-reference requests against the strategic roadmap (`research/Expected_features_speed_Assist_Product_Roadmap.md`). If a feature violates the core pivot (e.g., adding a heavy map module), flag it.
- **Create an Implementation Plan:** For any non-trivial change, AI must output an `implementation_plan.md` detailing:
  - Which layers (`data`, `domain`, `presentation`) will change.
  - What new classes or tests will be created.
- **Wait for Approval:** Do not write code until the user approves the plan.

## 2. Execution Phase (AI & Developer Workflow)
When executing a new feature, strict adherence to the following sequence is mandatory. **Do not make any assumptions, fail out loud, and ask for clarity.**

1. **Information Gathering:** Clarify requirements and gather any necessary mockups or existing references.
2. **Analysis:** Analyze the codebase to find where the feature fits cleanly without breaking existing logic.
3. **Preview (Diff Style):** Propose the exact code changes to the user using a `diff` style format. Clearly state the class names and functions being modified or created.
4. **Approval & Execution:** **Stop and wait.** Do not apply corrections or write the code until explicit approval is given by the user. Once approved, apply the exact changes.
5. **Post-Correction Review:** After applying the feature, show the resulting code changes using a `diff` style summary to confirm the exact modifications made.
6. **Module Separation (SDK Architecture):** Write logic in the appropriate module (`:speed-core`, `:speed-ui`, `:speed-overlay`, `:speed-autostart`, `:speed-bom`). Keep `:speed-core` headless with zero Compose dependencies.

## 3. Testing Phase (Mandatory)
Every new feature or bug fix MUST be accompanied by unit and/or UI tests.
- **Unit Tests:** Use **JUnit4 / Robolectric**, **MockK**, and **kotlinx-coroutines-test**. 
  - Domain telematics algorithms (`TelematicsEngine`, `SpeedWatcher`, `SpeedUnit`) and repository implementations must have high branch and line coverage (target > 90%).
  - **Verification:** Run `./gradlew testDebugUnitTest` locally to ensure all test suites pass before committing.
- **UI Tests:** Use **Compose Testing rules** (`createComposeRule`) to verify that UI elements render correctly based on specific `SpeedData` and `UiState` inputs.
- **CI/CD Quality Gates:** All commits and Pull Requests are automatically validated by GitHub Actions (`.github/workflows/quality-gates.yml`).

## 4. Verification & Documentation
- **Run Quality Gates:** Before concluding any task or pushing code, run the strict static analysis gates:
  - Run `./gradlew detekt lintDebug`
  - Fix any code smells or formatting issues reported by these tools.
- **Run the Build:** Always verify that the project compiles via `./gradlew assembleDebug`.
- **Update Docs:** If you added or modified public APIs, update the web documentation in `docs/` and verify the build with `npm run docs:build --prefix docs`.
- **Walkthrough:** Generate a `walkthrough.md` summarizing what was built, how it was tested, and how to verify the feature.


--- END OF FILE: standards/02_FEATURE_DEVELOPMENT_WORKFLOW.md ---


--- START OF FILE: standards/03_MAINTENANCE_AND_BUG_FIXING.md ---

# Maintenance & Bug Fixing

Guidelines for triaging, debugging, and resolving production issues (Bugs, ANRs, Regressions) safely.

## 1. Bug Fixing Protocol (AI & Developer Workflow)
When implementing a fix or addressing an issue, strict adherence to the following sequence is mandatory. **Do not make any assumptions, fail out loud, and ask for clarity.**

1. **Information Gathering:** Completely gather all necessary data before touching code. Ask the user for crash logs, system traces, or screenshots if they are required. The user can provide system traces for code if needed.
2. **Analysis:** Analyze the codebase deeply and identify the accurate, root-cause fix.
3. **Preview (Diff Style):** Propose the change to the user using a `diff` style format (or via an `implementation_plan.md` artifact). Clearly state the class name and function being modified.
4. **Approval & Execution:** Do not apply corrections until explicit approval is given by the user. Once approved, apply the exact changes.
5. **Post-Correction Review:** After applying the fix, show the resulting code changes using a `diff` style summary to confirm the exact modifications made.
6. **Verification:** Ask the user to check the fix on a physical device. Only mark the task as completed after on-device verification is successful.

## 2. Triage & Investigation
- **Trace the Source:** When presented with a stack trace (e.g., from Firebase Crashlytics), isolate the specific layer. Is it a UI crash? A background service exception? A location permission denial?
- **Avoid Guesswork:** Do not blindly wrap code in `try/catch`. Find the root cause (e.g., `NullPointerException` because GPS returned null before lock-on).

## 2. Fixing Application Not Responding (ANRs)
ANRs occur when the Main (UI) thread is blocked for > 5 seconds.
- **Rule:** Never perform I/O, database reads (Room/DataStore), or heavy computation (like filtering GPS arrays) on the Main thread.
- **Fix:** Move heavy work to `Dispatchers.IO` or `Dispatchers.Default` using Coroutines.
  ```kotlin
  withContext(Dispatchers.Default) {
      // heavy GPS math
  }
  ```

## 3. The Regression Testing Rule
Before fixing any reported bug, **you must write a failing test** that reproduces the bug.
1. Write a Unit Test that mimics the conditions of the crash. It should fail.
2. Implement the fix in the codebase.
3. Run the test again. It should pass.
This ensures the bug is caught in CI/CD and never returns.

## 4. Safe Refactoring
When modernizing legacy code (e.g., migrating an old XML Activity to Compose or refactoring the `SpeedometerService`):
- **Isolate:** Extract the business logic from the Android component into a decoupled class first.
- **Test:** Write tests for the decoupled logic.
- **Replace:** Swap the old implementation for the new one. Ensure zero functional changes from the user's perspective unless explicitly requested.


--- END OF FILE: standards/03_MAINTENANCE_AND_BUG_FIXING.md ---


--- START OF FILE: standards/04_NON_FUNCTIONAL_REQUIREMENTS.md ---

# Non-Functional Requirements (NFRs)

Because Speed Assist is a continuous-tracking app targeting safety and potentially fleets, Non-Functional Requirements are just as critical as the features themselves.

## 1. Battery & Resource Optimization
Continuous GPS polling is the #1 reason users uninstall driving apps.
- **Adaptive Polling:** Do not request high-accuracy 1-second GPS updates if the user is stationary for > 5 minutes. Downscale the request interval dynamically.
- **Wakelocks:** Use `ForegroundService` properly with clear notifications rather than raw CPU Wakelocks whenever possible. Release resources in `onDestroy()` or `onStop()`.
- **Auto-Start Efficiency:** Leverage `:speed-autostart` (Google Play Services `IN_VEHICLE` transition) for zero-friction background trip detection instead of continuous CPU wakelocks, saving massive battery power while waiting for trips to start.

## 2. Location & Privacy Compliance (Crucial)
- **Permissions:** Always handle permission degradation gracefully. If `ACCESS_BACKGROUND_LOCATION` is denied but foreground is granted, the app should still function while open.
- **Dialogs:** Adhere strictly to Google Play policies by showing explicit "Prominent Disclosure" rationale dialogs *before* requesting background location. (See `dialogs.showLocationPermissionRationale`).

## 3. Performance & Stability
- **Compose Recomposition:** Avoid passing unstable data classes or heavily mutating lists directly to Compose functions. Use `remember` and `key` blocks. Monitor for "jank" caused by excessive recomposition in HUD modes.
- **GPS Jitter (EMA & Schmitt Trigger):** Raw GPS data is noisy at low speeds. The app implements Exponential Moving Average (EMA $\alpha = 0.3$) smoothing and Dual Schmitt Trigger Hysteresis ($+1.0\text{ km/h} / -3.0\text{ km/h}$) to eliminate velocity jitter and prevent alarm fluttering at boundary limits.

## 4. Background Resiliency
- **OS Kill Prevention:** Android (Doze mode) aggressively kills background apps. Always utilize a highly optimized `ForegroundService` with a persistent, non-dismissible notification to prevent the OS from silently killing the app during a drive.

## 5. Safety & Distraction Optimization (Legal NFR)
- **Voice & Audio First:** The UI must not distract the driver. Once driving begins, the screen should require zero interaction. Rely on audio escalation and high-contrast, glanceable UIs (HUD mode).
- **Drive Mode Lockout:** Consider disabling complex UI interactions or typing while the vehicle is in motion to comply with hands-free and distraction laws.
- **HUD Mode:** The `HudDisplay` component enforces distraction safety by utilizing a high-contrast, pure OLED black (`#000000`) background intended strictly for windshield reflection during night driving, eliminating peripheral glare.

## 6. Hardware Heterogeneity Handling
- **Calibration Offset:** Different phones have varying GPS chip qualities, and car speedometers are intentionally calibrated to show faster speeds than reality. Allow users to manually adjust the app's speed calculation by a percentage offset to match their dashboard perfectly.

## 7. App Size & Offline Capability
- **Zero Cloud Reliance:** The core speed tracking and alerting must function 100% offline without an internet connection. Do not rely on cloud processing for real-time safety critical alerts.
- **Lightweight Footprint:** Total download size and runtime memory footprint must both remain $< 5\text{ MB}$.

## 8. SDK Modular Architecture (B2B Ecosystem)
Per the research failure analysis, the consumer app market is tough, and B2B SDK licensing is the future.
- **Core Independence:** The location tracking and speed calculation logic (`TelematicsEngine`, `SpeedWatcher`, `ISpeedRepository`) in `:speed-core` is completely decoupled with zero UI or ad dependencies.
- **Modular Mindset:** Features are isolated across `:speed-core`, `:speed-ui`, `:speed-overlay`, `:speed-autostart`, and `:speed-bom` with minimal public API surface.

## 9. App Startup & Launch Weight
- **Lightweight Initialization:** The app must open instantly. Do not initialize heavy SDKs, database migrations, or complex location requests synchronously on the main thread during `Application.onCreate()` or `Activity.onCreate()`. Defer non-essential initializations until after the first frame has rendered.


--- END OF FILE: standards/04_NON_FUNCTIONAL_REQUIREMENTS.md ---

# CI/CD, Code Quality & Release Pipeline

This document defines the automated quality gates, linting rules, test execution, and Maven publishing workflows for the **Veg Sahayyak SDK** codebase.

<BadgesBar />

---

## 🏗️ Continuous Integration Workflow

Every Pull Request and commit pushed to the `main` branch undergoes automated validation defined in `.github/workflows/quality-gates.yml`.

```mermaid
graph LR
    PR[Git Push / PR] --> LINT[Static Analysis<br/>Detekt & Android Lint]
    PR --> UNIT[Unit Tests & JUnit<br/>Robolectric & JUnit4]
    PR --> BUILD[AAR/BOM Build<br/>Release Variants]
    
    LINT --> GATE{Quality Gate Pass?}
    UNIT --> GATE
    BUILD --> GATE
    
    GATE -->|Success| RELEASE[GitHub Packages Maven Publish]
    GATE -->|Failure| BLOCK[Block Merge]
```

---

## 🔍 1. Static Analysis & Linters

The SDK enforces strict Kotlin coding standards, complexity limits, and architectural boundaries:

| Tool | Role | Command |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **`detekt`** | Identifies complexity smells, potential memory leaks, and architectural deviations. | `./gradlew detekt --stacktrace --info` |
| **`Android Lint`** | Scans for Android API deprecations, resource leaks, and manifest security flaws. | `./gradlew lintDebug --stacktrace --info` |

To run all static analysis checks locally before opening a pull request:

```bash
./gradlew detekt lintDebug
```

---

## 🧪 2. Internal Automated Test Suites

The core telematics algorithms (`TelematicsEngine`, `SpeedWatcher`, `SpeedometerService`) are covered by comprehensive JVM unit tests using **Robolectric** and **JUnit4**:

```kotlin
// Source: speed-core/src/test/kotlin/com/vegsahayyak/speedcore/domain/TelematicsEngineTest.kt
package com.vegsahayyak.speedcore.domain

import org.junit.Assert.assertFalse
import org.junit.Assert.assertTrue
import org.junit.Test

class TelematicsEngineTest {

    private fun assertSustainedSpeed(engine: TelematicsEngine, speedKmh: Float): TelematicsResult {
        var result: TelematicsResult? = null
        // Call processLocation multiple times to allow Exponential Moving Average (EMA) to converge
        repeat(15) {
            result = engine.processLocation(speedKmh / 3.6f, 10f)
        }
        return result!!
    }

    @Test
    fun `isOverLimit triggers hysteresis correctly`() {
        val engine = TelematicsEngine()
        engine.setWarningThresholdMps(100f / 3.6f)

        // Below limit (90 km/h) -> No alert
        var result = assertSustainedSpeed(engine, 90f)
        assertFalse(result.isOverLimit)

        // Exceeds limit by 2 km/h (102 km/h) -> Triggers alert
        result = assertSustainedSpeed(engine, 102f)
        assertTrue(result.isOverLimit)

        // Drops to limit (100 km/h) -> Still true due to hysteresis (-3 km/h buffer)
        result = assertSustainedSpeed(engine, 100f)
        assertTrue(result.isOverLimit)

        // Drops below hysteresis threshold (96 km/h < 97 km/h) -> Clears alert
        result = assertSustainedSpeed(engine, 96f)
        assertFalse(result.isOverLimit)
    }

    @Test
    fun `isUnderLimit triggers hysteresis correctly`() {
        val engine = TelematicsEngine()
        engine.setMinWarningThresholdMps(50f / 3.6f)

        // Above minimum (60 km/h) -> No alert
        var result = assertSustainedSpeed(engine, 60f)
        assertFalse(result.isUnderLimit)

        // Drops below minimum by 2 km/h (48 km/h) -> Triggers under-speed alert
        result = assertSustainedSpeed(engine, 48f)
        assertTrue(result.isUnderLimit)

        // Rises above hysteresis threshold (54 km/h > 53 km/h) -> Clears alert
        result = assertSustainedSpeed(engine, 54f)
        assertFalse(result.isUnderLimit)
    }
}
```

Run test suites locally:

```bash
./gradlew testDebugUnitTest --info
```

---

The SDK enforces a strict **90%+ coverage bar** on all domain logic:

* **Domain & Telematics Logic (`TelematicsEngine`)**: 100% branch coverage.
* **Location Signal Filtering (`SpeedWatcher`)**: 96% coverage.
* **Unit Conversions (`SpeedUnit`)**: 100% coverage.
* **Preferences & Service Locator**: 91% coverage.

Test results are uploaded via `mikepenz/action-junit-report@v4` on every pipeline run.

When a GitHub Release tag is published, `.github/workflows/publish-sdk.yml` automatically triggers:

This compiles and publishes the release artifacts to **GitHub Packages**:

--- START OF FILE: troubleshooting/index.md ---

# Troubleshooting & Common Edge Cases

Find solutions to common integration hurdles, Android OEM background battery killers, and QA testing strategies for the **Veg Sahayyak SDK**.

---

## 🛑 1. `ForegroundServiceStartNotAllowedException`

### Symptoms
App crashes on **Android 12+ (API 31+)** when calling `SpeedAssistant.with(context).start()` while the app is in the background.

```
Fatal Exception: android.app.ForegroundServiceStartNotAllowedException: 
Service.startForeground() not allowed due to mAllowStartForeground false
```

### Cause
Android 12 strictly forbids starting foreground services while an application is in the background, with limited exceptions (e.g. high-priority FCM pushes, exact alarms).

### Solution
Always invoke `start()` from an active foreground component (`Activity` or user interaction button), or verify `isAppInForeground`:

```kotlin
// Ensure start() is called when the driver is actively interacting with the UI
fun onStartTrackingClicked(activity: Activity) {
    if (SpeedPermissions(activity).hasPermission()) {
        SpeedAssistant.with(activity).start()
    } else {
        requestPermissions(activity)
    }
}
```

---

## 🔋 2. OEM Background Kills (Samsung, Xiaomi, Oppo)

### Symptoms
The status bar speed notification disappears or freezes after the device screen has been turned off for several minutes.

### Cause
Proprietary battery savers (Samsung Device Care, Xiaomi MIUI Battery Saver, Huawei PowerGenie) forcefully terminate background processes even if they run as foreground services.

### Solutions
1. **AutoStartManager (Recommended)**: Use the `:speed-autostart` module to leverage Google Play Services `IN_VEHICLE` transitions, which OEMs typically exempt from termination because they rely on the low-power sensor hub instead of CPU wakelocks.
2. **Request Battery Optimization Exemption**: Direct drivers to allow unconstrained background execution:
   ```kotlin
   val intent = Intent(Settings.ACTION_REQUEST_IGNORE_BATTERY_OPTIMIZATIONS).apply {
       data = Uri.parse("package:${context.packageName}")
   }
   context.startActivity(intent)
   ```
3. **Screen-Off Throttling**: Configure the SDK to pause GPS during screen-off cycles if full background tracking is not strictly needed:
   ```kotlin
   SpeedAssistant.with(context).preferences.setUpdateWhileScreenOff(false)
   ```

---

## 🛰️ 3. Simulating Telemetry in Android Emulator & Local QA

Testing speed thresholds and alerts without a physical vehicle can be done using the following verified methods:

### Option A: `FakeSpeedRepository` (Recommended for Local Dev & Tests)
For instant, deterministic speed simulation in ViewModels and Compose UI without waiting for GPS locks, use the [FakeSpeedRepository](/guide/testing#2-synthetic-telematics-fixture-fakespeedrepository):

```kotlin
val fakeRepo = FakeSpeedRepository()
SpeedAssistant.with(context).useRepository(fakeRepo).start()

// Emit 95 km/h over-speed violation
fakeRepo.emitSpeed(speedKmh = 95f, isOverLimit = true)
```

### Option B: Android Studio Emulator Extended Controls (GPX Route Playback)
1. Open Emulator **Extended Controls (...)** &rarr; **Location**.
2. Click **Routes** and load a `.gpx` or `.kml` GPS route file.
3. Set playback speed to **1.0x** or **2.0x** and click **Play Route**.
4. The emulator streams live GPS coordinates, allowing `FusedLocationProviderClient` and `SpeedGauge` to animate smoothly in real time.

### Option C: `setMockLocation()` Instrumentation
For programmatic end-to-end testing of `FusedLocationProviderClient` on test devices, see the [End-to-End GPS Mocking Guide](/guide/testing#5-end-to-end-gps-mocking-via-fusedlocationproviderclient).

## 🏃 4. AutoStartManager Not Triggering

### Symptoms
Trips are not starting automatically when the driver begins driving.

### Cause & Solution
* **Missing Google Play Services**: `AutoStartManager` relies on the Google Play Services Activity Recognition API. If the device does not have Play Services installed (e.g., AOSP or Huawei HarmonyOS devices), the `onError` callback will trigger with an `ApiException`.
* **Missing Permissions**: Ensure the `ACTIVITY_RECOGNITION` permission is granted (Android 10+).

---

## 🎙️ 5. Voice Command Parsing Fails

### Symptoms
The `VoiceCommandButton` spins or fails to parse actions like `VoiceAction.SetProfile`.

### Cause & Solution
* **Microphone Permission Denied**: Ensure `android.permission.RECORD_AUDIO` is requested and granted at runtime before launching the voice recognizer intent.
* **No Internet Connection**: The default Android `SpeechRecognizer` requires an active internet connection on older API levels to perform transcription. Handle offline scenarios gracefully.

---

## ❓ FAQ

### Does the SDK require Google Play Services?
Yes. The SDK leverages Google's `FusedLocationProviderClient` for optimal battery efficiency, and `AutoStartManager` requires the Activity Recognition API.

### Why doesn't the Minimum Speed alert fire immediately when starting from 0 km/h?
The `TelematicsEngine` incorporates a startup safety guard. To prevent continuous, annoying alarms while parked, at stoplights, or pulling out of a driveway, the under-speed alert is only armed after the vehicle has initially accelerated past **MinLimit + 3.0 km/h**.

### Can I override the default Notification layout?
Yes. You can supply custom notification channels and actions by interacting with `SpeedAssistant.with(context).setWarningPendingIntent(...)`.



--- END OF FILE: troubleshooting/index.md ---


--- START OF FILE: ui-components/index.md ---

# Jetpack Compose UI Components

The `:speed-ui` module provides drop-in, hardware-accelerated Jetpack Compose widgets designed for automotive dashboards, driver safety HUDs, and telematics settings screens.

---

## 🏎️ The `SpeedGauge` Component

`SpeedGauge` is a circular speedometer gauge rendering custom vector arcs, dynamic speed ticks, smoothed needle motion, and real-time GPS accuracy status.

<InteractiveSpeedGauge :initialSpeed="55" :initialLimit="80" initialUnit="km/h" />

---

## 📦 Basic Usage

```kotlin
import androidx.compose.runtime.Composable
import androidx.compose.ui.Modifier
import com.vegsahayyak.speedui.components.SpeedGauge
import com.vegsahayyak.speedui.components.ThemeMode
import com.vegsahayyak.speedcore.units.SpeedUnit

@Composable
fun SpeedometerScreen(
    currentSpeed: Float, 
    warningLimit: Float = 80f,
    minCorridorLimit: Float = 40f
) {
    SpeedGauge(
        speed = currentSpeed,
        warningSpeed = warningLimit,         // Maximum speed ceiling
        minSpeedLimit = minCorridorLimit,    // Minimum highway corridor
        isTrackingActive = true,
        isOverLimit = currentSpeed > warningLimit,
        themeMode = ThemeMode.DARK_GRAY,
        unitLabel = "km/h",
        showGpsAccuracy = true,
        gpsAccuracyMeters = 3.5f,
        onUnitSelected = { selectedIndex ->
            // Handle unit change (e.g. km/h vs mph)
        }
    )
}
```

---

## ⚙️ Component Parameters Reference

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `speed` | `Float` | **Required** | Current instantaneous vehicle speed. |
| `warningSpeed` | `Float` | **Required** | Maximum speed ceiling threshold. |
| `isTrackingActive` | `Boolean` | **Required** | Whether GPS tracking is actively running or in standby. |
| `isOverLimit` | `Boolean` | `false` | When true, renders red alert glowing tones and warning styles. |
| `modifier` | `Modifier` | `Modifier` | Modifier to be applied to the gauge container. |
| `minSpeedLimit` | `Float` | `0f` | Optional minimum speed corridor limit. |
| `maxSpeed` | `Float` | `180f` | Maximum dial scale value (e.g. 180 for km/h, 120 for mph). |
| `unitLabel` | `String` | `"km/h"` | Text label displayed beneath the digital readout. |
| `unitOptions` | `List<UiSpeedUnit>` | `UiSpeedUnit.entries` | Supported selectable units dropdown options (`KMH`, `MPH`, `MPS`, `FPS`). |
| `labelStep` | `Int` | `20` | Numeric interval between major dial tick marks. |
| `onUnitSelected` | `((Int) -> Unit)?` | `null` | Callback triggered when the driver taps the unit selector. |
| `themeMode` | `ThemeMode` | `ThemeMode.SYSTEM` | Color mode: `SYSTEM`, `DARK_GRAY`, `OLED_BLACK`, `HIGH_CONTRAST`. |
| `colorScheme` | `SpeedUiColorScheme?` | `null` | Optional custom client branding color scheme. |
| `showGpsAccuracy` | `Boolean` | `true` | Toggles the real-time GPS accuracy badge on/off. |
| `gpsAccuracyMeters` | `Float` | `-1f` | Precision in meters (≤ 5m Good, ≤ 20m Fair, > 20m Weak). |
| `isHudMirrored` | `Boolean` | `false` | When true, flips the gauge vertically for windshield reflection. |

---

## 🎨 Theme Modes & OLED Optimization

The `SpeedGauge` supports built-in theme presets configured via the `ThemeMode` enum:

```kotlin
enum class ThemeMode {
    SYSTEM,        // Automatically follows Android system Dark/Light mode
    DARK_GRAY,     // Deep charcoal gray background with vibrant accents
    OLED_BLACK,    // Pure true black (#000000) for maximum OLED battery savings
    HIGH_CONTRAST, // Ultra-high visibility yellow/white accents for direct sunlight
    HUD_MIRRORED   // Inverts and mirrors layout vertically for windshield projection
}
```

---

## 🎨 Custom Brand Color Schemes (`SpeedUiColorScheme`)

You can supply fully customized color palettes to `SpeedGauge` and `HudDisplay`:

```kotlin
val myBrandColors = SpeedUiColorScheme(
    safeColor = Color(0xFF00E676),
    warningApproachColor = Color(0xFFFF9100),
    overSpeedColor = Color(0xFFFF1744),
    underSpeedColor = Color(0xFF00E5FF),
    warningGlowColor = Color(0x88FF1744),
    needleColor = Color(0xFF2979FF)
)

SpeedGauge(
    speed = currentSpeed,
    warningSpeed = 80f,
    isTrackingActive = true,
    colorScheme = myBrandColors
)
```

---

## 🌙 HUD Mode & Windshield Reflection (`HudDisplay`)

The `HudDisplay` composable offers a dedicated, large-digit (120sp) night-driving display that reflects off a vehicle's windshield. It is strictly rendered against a pure OLED black (`#000000`) background to minimize battery drain and reduce peripheral glare distractions.

```kotlin
import com.vegsahayyak.speedui.components.HudDisplay
import com.vegsahayyak.speedui.components.HudMirrorAxis
import com.vegsahayyak.speedui.components.hudMirror

// Dedicated digital HUD composable
HudDisplay(
    speed = currentSpeed,
    warningSpeed = 80f,
    minSpeedLimit = 40f,
    isTrackingActive = true,
    isMirrored = true,
    unitLabel = "km/h",
    onMirrorToggle = { isMirrored -> /* toggle state */ }
)

// Or mirror any Composable using the hudMirror modifier
Box(modifier = Modifier.hudMirror(isMirrored = true, axis = HudMirrorAxis.VERTICAL)) {
    SpeedGauge(speed = currentSpeed, warningSpeed = 80f, isTrackingActive = true)
}
```

### High Contrast Mode for Daylight Driving

When commercial drivers operate in bright, direct sunlight, enable `ThemeMode.HIGH_CONTRAST` to boost needle visibility:

```kotlin
SpeedGauge(
    speed = currentSpeed,
    warningSpeed = 80f,
    isTrackingActive = true,
    themeMode = ThemeMode.HIGH_CONTRAST
)
```

## 🧩 Accessibility & Screen Readers

`SpeedGauge` implements Android Accessibility semantics out-of-the-box via `SpeedGaugeTokens.contentDescriptionFor(...)`. Screen readers (TalkBack) will announce contextual updates such as:

> *"Current speed 78 kilometers per hour, speed limit 80 kilometers per hour. Warning status: normal."*

---

## 🖼️ XML Layout & ViewBinding Interoperability

If your project is built with traditional XML layouts, you can embed `SpeedGauge` directly using AndroidX `ComposeView`:

```xml [res/layout/item_speedometer_card.xml]
<androidx.compose.ui.platform.ComposeView
    android:id="@+id/speedometerComposeView"
    android:layout_width="match_parent"
    android:layout_height="220dp" />
```

In your Activity or Fragment:

```kotlin
binding.speedometerComposeView.setContent {
    SpeedGauge(
        speed = currentSpeedKmh,
        warningSpeed = 80f,
        minSpeedLimit = 40f,
        isTrackingActive = true,
        isOverLimit = currentSpeedKmh > 80f
    )
}
```

---

## 🪟 The `PipWidget` Component (`:speed-overlay`)

`PipWidget` is a floating circular speedometer overlay designed to render over third-party applications (Google Maps, Waze, delivery apps) using `SYSTEM_ALERT_WINDOW`.

```kotlin
import com.vegsahayyak.speedoverlay.PipWidget
import com.vegsahayyak.speedoverlay.PipWidgetConfig

PipWidget(
    speed = currentSpeed,
    unitLabel = "km/h",
    isOverLimit = isOverLimit,
    isUnderLimit = isUnderLimit,
    config = PipWidgetConfig(
        size = 100.dp,
        safeColor = Color(0xFF1FC95E),
        warningColor = Color(0xFFE31D23)
    )
)
```

### `PipWidgetConfig` Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `size` | `Dp` | `100.dp` | Outer diameter of the circular floating bubble. |
| `safeColor` | `Color` | `0xFF1FC95E` | Outer border color when driving within normal limits. |
| `warningColor` | `Color` | `0xFFE31D23` | Outer border color during over-speed violations. |
| `underSpeedColor` | `Color` | `0xFF29B6F6` | Outer border color during under-speed violations. |
| `backgroundColor` | `Color` | `0x66000000` | Translucent glassmorphism background color. |
| `speedTextSize` | `TextUnit` | `36.sp` | Digital speed readout typography size. |
| `unitTextSize` | `TextUnit` | `14.sp` | Speed unit label typography size. |
| `textColor` | `Color` | `Color.White` | Text color for speed digits and unit. |

---

## 🎙️ The `VoiceCommandButton` Component (`:speed-ui`)

A Floating Action Button (FAB) that captures spoken audio from the driver and triggers speed limit adjustments hands-free.

```kotlin
import com.vegsahayyak.speedui.components.VoiceCommandButton
import com.vegsahayyak.speedui.api.VoiceAction

VoiceCommandButton(
    // parser defaults to null (uses built-in internal parser)
    onCommandParsed = { action ->
        when (action) {
            is VoiceAction.SetProfile -> {
                SpeedAssistant.with(context).setDrivingProfile(action.profile)
            }
            is VoiceAction.ChangeUnit -> {
                println("Switched unit to: ${action.unitName}")
            }
            is VoiceAction.Unknown -> {
                println("Unrecognized voice command")
            }
        }
    }
)
```
